entries.title: Chris's house: lived-in family-home details on every floor (dev)
items: Hall with coat rack, boots, wellies, umbrella and a mirror console; a wood-stove corner with an armchair, knitting basket, guitar, log basket and a cat that stares at the wall.

Family photo walls, an advent calendar whose doors open day by day, a clock, kitchen coffee + lefse + pepperkaker corner, plate rail and pot rack, posters, a Lego shelf, a toy box, a dollhouse and a spooky old trunk upstairs.
All of it sits clear of doors, stairs and the Christmas-tree spot, and it costs 3 draw calls.

entries.title: People no longer teleport (dev)
items: Townspeople only move at a human pace where you can see them: when someone would jump across the street (side switch, road change, nudged out of the road) he now walks there instead of popping across.
New people are placed only where you cannot see them (behind you or far away), and when the evening crowd shrinks nobody vanishes in front of you; they stay until they are out of sight.
A friend who joins a chat circle is no longer pulled across town while you can see him.
Carol singers who are asked to step out of the road now walk to the pavement together instead of dashing there.

entries.title: Creatures roam the woods and show on the map (dev)
items: At any time a few creatures (Huldra, Draugr, Tusser, Varulv, Lyktemann, Gjenganger, Fossegrim, Nøkken, Draugen, Lindorm, Edderkoppkongen, Rokk and, from day 20, the Wild Hunt) are out somewhere in the woods, on a spot that fits them: trees, bog, a lonely house, a stream bank, open water, a cave mouth, a bare peak. They move to a new spot every few minutes.

You can see them on the big map (N), layer CREATURES: bright pin, pulsing ring and name, also in the phone GPS and the search box. The minimap shows the ones within 700 m on its rim. The dim marker still shows where a creature was last seen.

When you walk to within about 120 m of one (at the right time of day, and only when nothing else is going on) it really appears there. Want it scarier? Layers panel: SCARY MODE hides them. (dev build only)

entries.title: Animals make you koselig (dev)
items: Your Koselig (Julestemning) meter now goes up when you feed animals (+3 each, deer, foxes, hares, strays), when a bird lands and sits on your hand (+4), and a little when birds peck seeds from your hand (+1). Up to 20 points a day from animals.

entries.title: Calm arms: no more flailing (dev)
items: People's arms no longer flail or spin. The bug: whenever someone raised their arms more than about 55 degrees (phone call, gasp, warming hands, gossip, running away, slipping on ice) the arms flipped sides and spun backwards every single frame. They now stay where they should.
Slipping on ice, brushing off dust, jogging on the spot, running away in panic and the carolers scattering all use smaller, slower arm movements (bent arms, no more windmilling over the head).
Chatting people make small, slower hand gestures with pauses in between, and waving is calmer.

entries.title: People just speak (dev)
items: No more speech-bubble text over people's heads when they talk: they just speak. (Add ?bubbles=1 to the address to see the bubbles again.)

entries.title: People at home have their colours back (dev)
items: The people sitting on the sofa, cooking, reading, dancing or walking around inside the houses were flat white blocks with no face or clothes. They now have their normal outfits, skin and faces, just like everyone else in town.

entries.title: Nothing floats: arena net and garden trees (dev)
items: The orange safety net round the airsoft arena now follows the ground all the way round instead of hanging in the air over dips and slopes.
The little lit Christmas trees in the gardens keep clear of the real trees: no more Christmas trees sitting on top of a canopy.

entries.title: Softer, nicer footsteps (dev)
items: Walking sounds are quieter and rounder: the sharp clicky top end is filtered off so hard floors no longer sound like typing on a keyboard, and the loudness varies less from step to step. They are still there, just not noticeable.
Driving no longer plays footsteps sped up to the speed of the car.

entries.title: Bridges are smooth to drive and walk (dev)
items: Fixed the invisible block in the middle of bridges: hedges that were built on bridge decks are gone, small bridges no longer arch up like a ramp, and walking over any bridge now follows the real deck height instead of 1 m steps.
Every bridge on the map was walked and driven end to end by a test, including the Hunsbedt bru to green bridge race route.

entries.title: Wood creatures: Wild Hunt, Mare and Lindorm (dev)
items: Åsgårdsreia, the Wild Hunt, thunders across the sky on the late Yule nights: an antlered leader on a skeletal black horse and three riders. Stay out of their stare and go indoors.
The Mare: sleep at night and she may visit. You wake at 03:12 and cannot move while she sits in front of you.
The Lindorm: a 9 m serpent coiled on rocky ground. Come close and it rises, hisses, strikes, then slithers off. Thunder, Tyr and iron hurt it.

entries.title: Wood creatures: Varulv, Spider King and Rokk (dev)
items: The Varulv: you hear him howl first, twice, then he stalks you through the dark trees. Look at him and he freezes; look away and he creeps closer. He gets likelier every day toward the full moon.
The Spider King lives in a giant web outside each troll cave. He drops on a silk thread, rears and skitters at you, then climbs back up.
The Rokk: a giant eagle. Its shadow crosses the snow first, then it circles and dives. Get under trees or indoors and it leaves.

entries.title: Wood creatures: Nøkken, Draugen, Lyktemann and Gjenganger (dev)
items: The Nøkken: a pale water man standing in the shallows with his back to you. Look at him too long and he turns his head all the way round, then sinks; a ripple races to the shore nearest you and a long webbed hand comes up out of the water at the edge. Laguz and iron hurt him.
The Draugen is now a real headless sailor in a rotten half-boat, rowing through the fog with a green lantern. Close to the shore he turns, glides in, points at you and sinks.

The Lyktemann: a hooded lantern man in the woods who leads you off toward the water. Follow him and the lantern goes out. The Gjenganger: a see-through dead man in his Sunday suit who walks to the nearest house and knocks three times.
All four show on the map (CREATURES layer) and can be fought with runes: the sun rune is strong against all but the Nøkken.

entries.title: Kvent: new opponents, card packs, ladder, online
items: Kvent opponents all over town: Ingeborg the librarian (library counter) and Brit the shopkeeper (shop counter) play when you press E; Gunvald (Rødnisser chief) and Stempelsen (Blånisser chief) sit at card tables in front of their halls; the Frost Troll at a table outside the troll cave; the Witch beside her cauldron (she wants you to have beaten a few players first, and she eats cookies: every win makes her deck stronger).
The clans remember you: friends of a clan get 50% more kroner and cheaper clan packs; if you are a friend of the rival clan, or stole from the gift pile, the chief refuses to play.

Card packs: win matches for packs (a first win over each player, every third win, now and then a single card) or buy them; opening has a tear-and-flip animation. Duplicates are sold on the spot, so nothing is wasted. The deck builder only lets you use cards you own.
Your phone Kvent app now has a Ladder (record, locked/ready, clan standing), Card packs, My cards and Friends online.
Every opponent talks during the match (Norwegian or English, switch in the Kvent menu) and has a portrait.

Online Kvent: challenge Marius, Chris or Martin, play a move and answer whenever (play-by-mail). Works inside this browser now; the real relay is written but not switched on yet. Playing a friend or saying Good game gives Christmas spirit.
Kvent works on a phone: tap to play, landscape or portrait.

entries.title: Map music: every part of the map has its own feeling (dev)
items: The music now changes as you walk, drive or fly: the church and graveyard get chant and religious drones, the Rodnisser woods warm medieval folk, the Blanisser woods airy atmospheres, the troll caves deep low drones, the witch's house eerie wails, the plateau and frozen lake wide windy drones, mountains thin drones, the fjord cold drones, bridges soft river atmospheres, and the dark deep woods a dark bed. Each zone has day, night and storm versions.

Zones blend smoothly (equal-power crossfades by distance, no cuts). Kvinesdal town centre keeps the merry theme and the carols. The car radio, nisse village music, arenas, the Ninja venue, carols, the witch and the dark scare bed all take over from it and give it back afterwards.

Settings has a new Map music ON/OFF button and a volume slider. Marius can open music_zones.html (on the dev server) to click a zone on the map, play its tracks, pick new ones and paint new circle or polygon zones, then press SAVE.

entries.title: Rune magic: spells as well as weapons (dev)
items: Ten Norse runes you can cast as well as using weapons: ISA ice (freezes things, and grows an ice bridge when you aim at water), KAUN fire, THURS force push, SOL a small sun that lights the dark and burns the dead, NAUD a ward that eats hits, TYR lightning from the sky (outdoors only), LAGU a healing spring that puts out fires, HAGAL a hail storm, FEHU charm (calms animals, charms people for a moment), and MYRK the witch's dark rune. Each rune has 3 levels.

A MANA bar sits under your hearts: it refills slowly, slower in the dark and quicker by light. Every rune has its own cooldown. Tap I to cast the selected rune, HOLD I for the RUNE WHEEL (move the mouse, release to cast; 1-0 cast straight away). PS5: hold L1 for the wheel (stick or d-pad picks, release L1 or X casts, circle closes). Phone: tap the rune button.

Spells hurt and kill through the same system as weapons: draugr burn, huldra hates fire and sun, goblins flee the flames, trolls need lightning, hollows fear the sun. Killing people with magic counts exactly like using a weapon; fire next to a house is arson; dark magic costs Nice List points and Julestemning; charming people costs a little. Kids can never be hit. ?violence=0 makes spells harmless to living things (ice, light, ward and spring still work), ?magic=0 turns magic off.

You learn runes from carved RUNE STONES (the church, the troll caves, deep in the woods, and a dark one near the witch's lair: press G or tap), from the Rødnisser (Kaun, Thurs, Fehu) and the Blånisser (Ísa, Laguz, Hagall) as you bring them porridge, and from the Fossegrim (Nauð) if you stay and listen. Each clan dislikes the other's magic. Finding a rune again makes it stronger. The rune stones are on the big map (RUNE STONES layer) and in the GPS search. Dev build only.

entries.title: Walking, sprinting and jumping now feel like Minecraft (dev)
items: On foot: walk 4.3 m/s, sprint 5.6 m/s (click the left stick, hold Ctrl or double-tap W), sneak 1.3 m/s (hold Circle or Shift, you never walk off an edge). The picture widens a little when you sprint. Tilt the stick lightly to walk slower.
Jumping is a real 1.25 m jump (about half a second in the air) and a sprint-jump carries you about 4 m. Fixed: on roads the jump used to drop you from the top of the jump in one go.
Steep hills slow you down a little going up (never going down). A sword in your hand barely slows you, a gun a little more, and aiming a gun slows you the most.
Legs, footsteps and the head bob now match how fast you really go, so no more sliding feet. The Controls screen and the phone button (SPRINT) say the new buttons.

entries.title: Creatures, nisse villages and more are on the map (dev)
items: The big map (N) has new layers: CREATURES (Huldra H, Draugr D, Fossegrim F, Tusser T: bright with a pulsing ring when one is out there right now, dim where each was last seen), NISSER (red hat = Rødnisser village, blue hat = Blånisser village), WILDLIFE NOW (animals around you) and MORE PLACES (the witch's lair, Rusty, the barn, the airsoft arena, bridges). All are on by default.

The minimap shows creatures and animals near you, and a red / blue dot on its rim with the distance when a nisse village is out of view. You can zoom the big map out far enough to see the whole world with padding.

Creatures, nisse villages and the extras are in the phone GPS (categories CREATURES, NISSER, MORE PLACES) and in the search box, so you can set a GPS target on them. Want a scarier game? Layers panel: SCARY MODE hides creatures and nisser everywhere. (dev build only)

entries.title: Airsoft Arena next to Bowlinghallen (dev)
items: East of Bowlinghallen, in the open field with the tree cluster: an airsoft arena with orange safety netting, crates, barrels, tyres, plywood walls and a shipping container, and Dommer the referee in his hut. Press G next to Dommer. (dev build only)

Shop: softgun pistol, SMG and sniper, bags of 500 small white round BBs, goggles, a team armband and hip / chest / back holsters (quick draw, and you can see them on yourself in third person). Everything lands in your inventory.

Skirmish: you and three bots against four bots, four minutes. A hit means out for 10 seconds (hands up, nobody shoots you), live score and a scoreboard at the end, and a payout (win 300, draw 120, loss 50 kr, plus 5 kr per hit). Goggles are required. The white BBs really fly, bounce off cover and lie on the ground afterwards. Nobody is hurt, nobody calls the police.
Left click fires (hold for full auto on the SMG), right click aims (the sniper has a scope), R reloads from your BB bags. No fire inside the safe zone around the hut.

entries.title: More voices: the town talks a lot more (dev)
items: New: about 1400 new spoken lines, around two thirds of them in Norwegian. Townspeople, nisser (red and blue clans), police, kids and old folk now comment on the weather, the time of day, the Advent day, the Nice List, your mood, riding, the race, the Kvent card game, the snowball arena and Posten deliveries.
Nobody repeats themselves any more: every group of lines plays all of its lines before any line comes round again, and never the same line twice in a row.
Lines that used to be text only (narrator, radio, shops, phone texts, the lantern) now have a voice too. They are computer voices for now, ready to be re-recorded in the recording studio.
Recorded lines now stay on screen for as long as the recording lasts, so a longer take is never cut off.

entries.title: Posten: a delivery job (dev)
items: New: a job at Posten. Talk to the postmaster at the red Posten stand by the post office (Kvinesdal post i butikk) to get hired: you get a Posten cap, jacket and bag you can wear (cap + jacket = bigger tips).

Each round is 4 to 8 parcels for named villagers at real house doors around town (more parcels the later in advent). The phone has a new Posten app with the route list; each parcel is a pin on the map and a GPS target.

At the door press E to ring the bell: the villager opens, says a line in Norwegian and tips you if you are fast. At the end you get a shift summary with 0 to 3 stars, your wage in kr, Nice List points and a rank (Lærling, Brevbærer, Postbud, Postmester).
Still to come: Posten van and bike, sled, dogs and icy roads, wrong addresses, the Christmas Eve run. ?post=0 turns it off.

entries.title: Julestemning: your Christmas spirit (dev)
items: New: a second meter under the Nice List, Julestemning (Christmas spirit), 0 to 100 with five moods: Grinch, Gnurten, Fin, Koselig and Julemagi. Tap it for the full card, or find it in the phone menu.

Warm fires, gløgg, pepperkaker, carols, the radio, friends nearby, decorating, a good sleep, games, snow play and good deeds raise it. Freezing cold, hunger, scary nights, storms, the police, being hurt and bad deeds lower it.

Low spirit turns you into a funny Grinch: the world goes grey-green, the Christmas music sags two semitones and you grumble. High spirit gives a golden glow, sparkles, faster warming and the odd lucky coin.

It never drops below 8 and never punishes you: after ten gloomy minutes a nisse, your mum or Lykta cheers you up. The Nice List race shows everyone's mood. Add ?spirit=0 to the address to turn it off.

entries.title: Riding: horses, reindeer, deer and a very moody moose
items: Feed a horse, reindeer or deer until it shows a heart, then press G next to it (pad Square, RIDE button on phones) to climb on. G again gets off. You need a saddle: the Fôr og Dyr stall sells them (180 kr).

Steer with the move stick or W A S D: forward goes (walk, then trot), Shift / Ctrl / L3 / RUN gallops (it tires the animal, a bar shows its stamina), S brakes and backs up slowly, Space / Cross jumps. The camera turns with the animal and hooves thump on every step.
Each animal has its own speed and jump: the horse is fastest and steady, the reindeer is gentle and tireless, the deer is quick and jumps highest and sometimes spooks.

The moose can carry you after lots of feeding but it is slow, tires fast, spooks sideways, warns you, and finally bucks you off. Hold a carrot or apple and right click in the saddle to give a treat (stamina back).

entries.title: Two nisse clans in the woods: Rødnisser and Blånisser (dev)
items: Far out in the woods live two rival julenisse clans with their own cave villages: the Rødnisser (red hats, lively fiddle) far north-west and the Blånisser (blue hats, slow and airy) far south-east. Each has a Great Hall you can walk into, tiny houses, mailboxes, a fire, lanterns and knee-high nisser who fetch firewood and carry gifts. (dev build only)

You hear them singing long before you see them (real recorded kulning, 3D positioned), and Norwegian folk music fades in as you come close. Press G next to a nisse to talk (Norwegian voice and English subtitles). Bring rice porridge with butter to win a clan over, but the other clan will not like it. Taking gifts from their pile has consequences.
New car radio station FOLK FM (R cycles to it) with Norwegian folk fiddle and medieval music.

entries.title: Woods creatures: Huldra, Draugr, Fossegrim and Tusser (dev)
items: Four creatures from Norwegian folklore now haunt the woods at night (dev build only): the Huldra, a forest girl with a hollow bark back and two crows who beckons you on and walks away; the Draugr, a dead farmer who rises from his barrow with a rusty scythe and lumbers after you; the Fossegrim, a gaunt fiddler whose beard is a waterfall; and the Tusser, grumpy goblins round a campfire who scatter when you come close.
Every creature is one solid connected body in every pose, checked by an automatic test. In the Scares panel you can fire each one now: Huldra girl, Draugr, Fossegrim, Tusser.

entries.title: Kvent corner and a Christmas Bowlinghallen
items: Behind the lanes in Bowlinghallen: a Kvent corner with six tables. Four pairs of locals play each other (cards land, they say Ooh! and Scorch!), Pins-Per plays alone (press E to play him), and one empty table "Spill mot en venn" lets you challenge Marius, Chris or Martin (online play is a mock for now).

A big carved Kvent sign (lettering now always fits inside the sign, crisp at 2x) centred on the west wall above the tables, a smaller one on the counter wall, a tournament poster, a ladder poster and a how-to card.
The hall is brighter and cozier at all hours: ceiling pendant lamps and panels, neon signs, garlands, wreaths, lit trees and candles.

Outside: a glowing roofline, icicle lights, lit windows and doors, a Santa-hat bowling pin and star on the roof, a lit BOWLING sign with snow, trees with gifts, a snowman, a reindeer sleigh and candy-cane path lights.

entries.title: Wreck it!
items: Drive into things and they break: bins tip over and spill their rubbish, mailboxes pop off their posts, snowmen burst, gnomes crack, fences fly apart, bus stop glass sprays, lamp posts bend, market stalls collapse and Christmas trees lose their baubles.

Each smash scores Chaos points (+10 Bin! +25 Mailbox!) and quick smashes in a row make a combo. The faster you drive, the more flies. People shout when you wreck their things, and the Nice List does not like vandals.
Everything is put back after about ten minutes. Add ?wreck=0 to the address to switch it all off.

entries.title: Kvent plays like classic Gwent (dev)
items: Changed: Kvent now follows the classic card game rules line by line: 10 cards and 2 redraws, no new cards between rounds, ties cost both players a heart (Blånisser win them), spies end in the graveyard of the side they stood on, and leaders work once per match.

New: 18 leader powers (4 per faction), a 5th faction Fjord Folk, and a menu setting for who starts rounds 2 and 3 (default: the winner of the last round). The rules page and tutorial teach the classic rules. Ready-made decks are now 25-30 cards.

entries.title: Good deeds you can play (dev)
items: New: you can now earn Nice List points with real little activities, not only by luck. Shovel the snow outside a neighbour's door (orange flag), carry an old lady's groceries home from the shop, return lost mittens, wallets, keys and teddies to their owners, free a stuck fox, hare or deer, feed hungry stray cats and dogs, sit and talk with a lonely neighbour, call Mamma from the phone, and walk a frightened villager home at night.

Also: light the unlit street lanterns at dusk (matches: a stick plus coal), help a neighbour hang a wreath and lights, leave rice porridge at the little nisse doors at the edge of the woods (it is gone in the morning, and a small gift is left), play Kvent fair to the end, finish the street race without crashing, bring Uncle Rusty a hot meal, and sing carols yourself at the carol stands (press in time with Stille natt).

Every activity has a small prompt (E / tap / Square), a speech bubble with a Norwegian voice line, and a daily limit on points. ?gooddeeds=0 turns them all off. Testers: __GOOD.list() and __GOOD.start("name") jump to any of them.

entries.title: Find every Kvent player
items: Type "kvent" (or "kort", "cards", or a name) in the phone GPS search or the map search: every card player is listed. Pick one for Go (route), Teleport (3 m in front of them) and your record. Players not in town yet show "soon".
New Kvent app on the phone: Friends (Chris and Martin, Challenge opens the challenge screen), all card players by distance, your record and cards won.
New map layer KVENT: a small card icon on the minimap and big map for every card player in town.

entries.title: Santa's Nice List (dev)
items: New: your good and bad deeds now count on Santa's Nice List, and you can see your exact score every day. Press L, tap the star at the top, or open the phone and pick Nice List.

The list shows your score and tier (Angel, Nice, Naughty, Coal), what changed today, your last 10 deeds with the reason, the days left to the 24th, and a race between Marius, Chris and Martin with exact numbers.

Every deed is written down in full, so on Christmas Eve Santa can say why the winner won and how someone ended up with coal. Each kind of deed has a daily limit, so nobody can win by repeating one thing.
Each morning a line tells you yesterday's score, and there is a small kind errand of the day (+5). Feeding animals, jobs, quests, tipping carol singers and sharing cookies now count.

entries.title: Kvent, the card game, is in the game (first version)
items: Kåre the card player stands right in front of you when the game starts: press E (tap, or Square on the pad) to play Kvent with him. The cafe clerk (Sven) and the baker (Ola) play too.
Win and you get kroner and a pack of new cards for your collection; the townsperson gets a funny line either way. Esc, the X button or Circle takes you back to the game. Dev only.

entries.title: Many more spoken lines, and no repeats
items: Townspeople, nisse clans, the street race, guns and police, creatures, Kvent, advent days, weather and time of day all have new Norwegian lines, and anything you did (run, crash, wait) gets a reaction.
Every line pool now plays all its lines before it repeats, and never the same line twice in a row.
Lines that were only text before (sleep, mum's letters, NAF, radio) now have a voice. Dev only.

entries.title: Nights get darker as you leave town
items: The NIGHT slider (Settings > Time and weather) now means NIGHT WOODS. Near houses and in town the night stays bright, and as you walk out into the woods it fades slowly (about 15 to 25 seconds) down to the slider value (10 to 50 % is good). Walking back into town brightens it quicker.

entries.title: Kvinesdal Street Race
items: A real race on the real roads: from Hunsbedt bru through the valley and town to the old green steel footbridge at Krågehølen. Walk to the start gantry at Hunsbedt bru and press R (or tap the sign). There is a return race too.

Countdown with lights, 6 checkpoints with split times, boost pads, 4 computer cars, a ghost of your best run, medals (author, gold, silver, bronze) and prize money. R = respawn at the last checkpoint, T = instant restart, Esc = leave.
No police, no wanted stars: the route is closed while you race (traffic and pedestrians are cleared). If you are in a car you race it; otherwise a red race car is handed to you at the start.

entries.title: Driving that feels like GTA
items: New car handling: weighty and responsive, grip that drops on snow and ice, big handbrake slides (Space or R1) with a counter-steer assist, strong ABS brakes, bouncier crashes.
Chase camera with lag, speed FOV and swing into drifts, speed lines, skid marks and tyre smoke, engine and tyre sounds that follow the car. Pick GTA V, GTA IV, SIM or OLD in settings under DRIVING.
Controller: R2 gas, L2 brake and reverse, R1 handbrake, Create changes camera, hold triangle to get back on the road; rumble for slides, kerbs and crashes.

entries.title: The woods at night got scary (dev)
items: A hidden tension meter now decides when scary things happen: it rises when you are alone in the dark woods at night, far from lamps and houses, and drops by a warm light, a house or other people.

In the dark woods the calm music fades away and a dark low sound bed takes over (made only from the recordings you picked); it gets lower and heavier as the tension grows. Every few minutes the whole world goes silent for a few seconds, then a twig snaps.

New: the Follower. Footsteps in the snow behind you that stop when you stop. Later (day 6+) a dark shape at the edge of the flashlight that is closer every time you turn back, and (day 13+) you hear it breathing right behind you. It never hurts you.

Every scare now has the same shape: something feels wrong, a sound behind you, a long wait, then (sometimes nothing). The running shadow stays. The passive sightings (wisps, mittens, panda...) are almost gone. Scary moments: Gentle removes the hits and the breathing.

entries.title: Guns
items: Three guns exist now: a six-shot revolver, a double-barrel shotgun and a hunting rifle with a scope (hold right-click). Ammo is scarce: the hardware shop sells a few cartridges, chests and caves hide more. R reloads.
Every shot kicks hard: the gun and the camera jump, there is a bright muzzle flash, smoke, brass and a very loud bang that echoes across the valley. After the shotgun your ears ring.
The woods hear it. After dark a shot makes the strange things come sooner, and the town runs, screams and calls the police. Reloading in the dark is slow and fumbling.
Be careful where you point it. Nobody is hurt for real (people are knocked out, animals run), but the town remembers, and children can never be hit.

entries.title: Proper jump scares and pitch-black houses
items: Six new scary moments in the woods at night: the Tall One lunge (footsteps behind you, you turn, it is right there), a running shadow, a fake-out silence where something may or may not happen, footsteps that follow you and stop when you stop, scary figures that peek from behind trees (one, a group, or one that walks beside you), and the Predator: a squirrel, a few seconds of silence, a monster eats it and comes for you. It is fast but you can outrun it, scare it with the flashlight, or get indoors. Nothing here can kill you.

The barn and the empty house up the road are now pitch black at any time of day: only the flashlight (L) shows anything. A faint match glow appears if the flashlight is off. In there: a figure at the edge of the beam that is gone when lit, a pale face, a flickering beam, a slammed door.

Pause menu has a new button: Scary moments On / Gentle / Off (Gentle removes the jump scares, the predator and the flashes). ?scares=0 turns everything off, ?scares=gentle starts gentle. ?violence=0 means no blood from the Predator.

entries.title: Scare settings panel
items: Settings has a new SCARES section: on/off, presets (NORMAL / OFTEN / CONSTANT), a chance slider, a cooldown slider, a share slider per kind of sighting with its live percentage, and a button to fire any sighting right now. It is saved on your device.

entries.title: Woods sightings are much more frequent and have sounds
items: In the dev game a sighting can show up about 15 seconds after you start and every 25 seconds or so after that (the public game keeps the slow rare timing).
Every sighting now plays a sound when it appears (creep, terror, bells, crows, wind, doors).
Sightings no longer need trees nearby in the dev game. If something blocks one, a message on screen says why.

entries.title: Night darkness slider
items: Settings > Time and weather has a NIGHT slider (10-120 %). Lower = darker nights, so the flashlight does the work. It starts at 100 % (how the game looked before).

entries.title: The banishment scene keeps the house
items: Fixed: when the witch banishes you, Chris's house and the street around it no longer vanish in the middle of the scene (the start-at-the-town-hall spawn was pulling the world away).

entries.title: The barn log comes alive
items: Walk into the barn at Valløyna for the first time and the player says: "Well, here lies Hankie the Christmas log. Rest in peace, little buddy." (Chris and Martin each in their own voice). Afterwards the line only comes back now and then, and the old barn jokes play as before.

Then the pile twitches. A Santa hat pokes out, and Kåre the Christmas Log climbs up: a small round brown log with a red Santa hat, red mittens, a candy-cane scarf and big sparkly eyes. He wobbles, hops off the pile, waves, shouts a greeting in a tiny overexcited voice (one of five, some in Norwegian) and wanders off into the snow, saying a happy goodbye on the way.
A one-time surprise per save. It never blocks the barn door or the pile, costs nothing until you are near the barn, and is off with ?barnlog=0.

entries.title: Carolers sing, then the witch storms out
items: When the carolers reach Chris's house they now really sing for a while (you get a message when they start). Only after a full song does the witch storm out, shriek and chase them off with her broom.
The witch waits until you are close enough to see it, so the show is no longer wasted when you are far away.

entries.title: Strange things in the woods
items: Now and then, when you walk alone in the forest at dusk or night, something uncanny shows up for a few seconds and is gone when you look at it, walk up to it or look away. It never touches you.
The Tall One (Skogvokteren): a thin, faceless figure with bare twig antlers, standing between the trees. Look away and it may be closer.

Will-o'-the-wisps (lysglytt), a Huldra with a cow tail walking away from you, a trail of one red mitten and small footprints, bare footprints that just stop, a snowman that is closer every time you look, a cabin window that is not there when you turn back, a headless sailor in half a boat on the fjord, and a figure standing very still on the frozen river.
They are rare on purpose: at least six minutes between them, never in the town, never during cutscenes. The Panda is part of the same mix.

entries.title: Swords, pans and spears in the chests, and everything that lives can be hit
items: New things to find in chests and crates: a pancake pan (Pannekakepanne), club, hatchet, spear, hockey stick, snow shovel, ice axe, fish knife, candlestick, and in the caves and on the summits wooden, stone and iron swords, a bone sword, an icicle sword and a battle axe.

Animals and townspeople can now be hit. Animals fall over and leave meat, hide, wool, feathers or antlers (the grocery, clothes shop and hardware shop buy them). People drop a few kroner. Children cannot be hurt, and shopkeepers only get knocked out, then they are angry.
The town notices what you do, and so do the police. Be careful out there.

entries.title: Swords and tools look like Minecraft, and hitting feels like hitting
items: Every sword, axe, pickaxe, torch, lantern, flashlight, bell, sling, snowball and rocket is now a chunky 16x16 pixel item, held big in the lower right of the screen like Minecraft, with a raise-up when you switch and a quick diagonal slash when you swing. In third person the character holds the same item.

Hits now have weight: the swing freezes for a moment, the target flashes, gets knocked back and leans, little pixel chips fly (red for creatures, wood chips for trees, snow, grey sparks), the screen shakes a little, and a hit thud plays. Falling onto something is a critical hit with stars.
A small bar under the crosshair fills while your weapon recharges; swing too early and you hit weaker. The sword leaves a white slash arc, and chopping a tree now shows cracks and flying chips.

entries.title: Trolls you can actually see, in the caves and around them
items: Cave trolls now glow: bigger, brighter eyes you can spot from far down the tunnel, a green moss tint so they stand out from the blue rock, and a lantern burning beside every troll home. You hear a low growl a moment after you step in.
Cave 3 now has trolls waiting 20 to 40 metres inside, like the others.

A few trolls now also shuffle and lurk on the snow outside the mouths of the two far caves (up to 100 metres out). They only watch and grumble: they never attack. The cave close to town keeps its trolls inside.

The trolls are dangerous now: they notice you at about 14 m, raise the club and roar at about 9 m, and swing at about 3 m. Get bludgeoned and you wake up in the hospital (with the usual bill) and a dry word from Lykta. No gore, nothing is lost. Back off and they give up and walk home. ?trollsafe=1 turns the violence off.

You can fight back: the sword takes 12 hits and the axe 24 to topple a troll, snowballs only make them flinch and angry. A fallen troll breaks into snow and rock, may drop Orens or a rare Troll Penny, and comes back later (cave trolls on your next visit, outside trolls the next evening).

entries.title: Hollow people in the Threshold have glowing red eyes
items: In the Threshold World the grey townspeople now have two small red dots for eyes that glow, and the nearest ones throw a faint red light on the snow.

entries.title: The witch moves with her laugh
items: Her mouth now opens with each "ha" of her real laughs and closes in the pauses, instead of flapping at random. She throws her head back on the loud bursts, her shoulders and arms shake, and her eyes flare.
On her broom the silhouette bounces, tilts back and shudders with every cackle, and her glow pulses. When she screams her mouth opens wide and holds for the whole scream.

entries.title: Townspeople face the right way, plus named faces
items: The new townspeople now face the way they walk: pram pushers, kick-sled riders and dog walkers stand behind their things again.
The crowd has slim and stocky people, stooped old folk and things in their hands (mugs, bags, umbrellas, shovels, canes).
The bronze statue and the people on the trails use the new look too; Chris, Martin, Silje, Gudrun, Emil, Fru Ragnhild and the shop owners have their own faces and clothes.

entries.title: New look for the townspeople
items: Everybody in town now has the chunky look of Uncle Rusty: big heads, real faces, bobble hats, beards, aprons, scarves, uniforms and coats, built from the same set of parts so the town stays light.
The baker, the police, the shop staff, the carol singers, the skaters, the taxi passengers and the arena bots all got the new look; the same person always looks the same.
Dev switch in the movie panel: People: NEW / TODAY (or ?people=old).

entries.title: The witch really laughs
items: The witch now has real, dark cackles: twenty different laughs cut from a recording. She laughs them out as she flies over the valley, one after another with a few quiet seconds between, and the sound follows her across the sky.
She also laughs inside her flat. If you are outside her walls it comes through muffled and quieter.

entries.title: Everything in the houses you build can be used
items: Furniture you place in the builder now works like the furniture in the other houses: press G at a bed to sleep, at a toilet to flush, at a sink, shower or bath, a fridge for a snack, a lamp to switch the lights, a fireplace, piano or guitar.

New things to do: sit on sofas and chairs, browse bookshelves, open wardrobes (sometimes there is a coin in a pocket), use a computer, run on the treadmill, lift weights, read the time on a clock, shake a snow globe.
Chris's house is covered too: the toilet, shower, hot tub, sinks, fridge, sofas, bed, lamps, washing machine, gym and the punch bag upstairs. The bowling hall toilets and sinks work as well.

A bed you built saves the game, like Chris's bed. Sleeping it off clears the drunk meter, you cannot go to bed while you are passing out, and when you are drunk Rusty's camper sofa lets you sleep it off beside his door (sometimes for a 30 kr sofa fee).

entries.title: The animals are blocky again
items: The animals are back to their original chunky box look. The smoother Blender animals are still there if you want them: switch Animals to NEW in the movie panel.

entries.title: The Christmas tree goes where it should
items: The little Christmas tree that already stood in Chris's living room is gone: you bring the tree, and it goes exactly where that one stood, by the north wall next to the table.

Baubles, star, lights, tinsel and Mamma's special baubles now hang on the real branches of the tree you bought, whatever size you chose (small, medium or large). Lights spiral up the tree and blink, tinsel hangs draped around it, the star sits on top.

entries.title: The witch rides a broom
items: Sometimes, mostly at dusk and at night, the witch flies across the valley on her broom: a black silhouette with a crooked hat, glowing green eyes and a trail of green sparks, with a faint green glow on the snow below.
You hear her cackle from far away, the neighbours point and shout "Så du det?!", the birds scatter and the street lamps flicker as she passes. Look for her against the moon.
She only goes out when you are away from her house, and she gets bolder and lower the closer it gets to Christmas.

entries.title: The snowmen can talk
items: When you press G on a hatless snowman it now speaks, not only a subtitle: 49 lines, with a few different cheerful voices (the king is posh, the graveyard and cinema ones whisper).
The voice comes from the snowman's place, quieter the further away, and never talks over Lykta or the narration.
The old narrator-style hints (no hat, wrong hat, ask Fru Ragnhild) are now said by the snowman himself.

entries.title: Beer, wine and gløgg in the shops
items: The shops now sell alcohol, Norwegian style: lettøl and pils at Extra, the kiosks and the fuel stops (pils only until 8 pm), and julebokk, red and white wine, akevitt and bottled gløgg-vin at Vinmonopolet (inside the Extra building on Elvevegen, open 9 to 8).
Gløggboden sells a hot gløgg med skudd that warms you up, and the cafes and the stall sell a non-alcoholic gløgg (uten alkohol).

Buy it, put it in the hotbar and click to drink: it feeds the drunk meter. Bottles have several glasses, and empty cans and bottles go in the trash bins. The shopkeepers tease you when you are tipsy and refuse to sell when you are drunk.
Settings > Realism > Alcohol and drunk effects: one switch hides all alcohol in the shops and turns the drunk effects off.

entries.title: Fog is now a rare treat
items: Fog weather used to roll in far too often. It now shows up only now and then, and it is much lighter, so you can see the town.

entries.title: Uncle Rusty and his camper
items: A new neighbour has parked his old motorhome beside Chris's house: Uncle Rusty, an English relative in a tartan bathrobe and a woolly bobble hat, holding a beer in a permanent toast. The camper is covered in mud and blinking Christmas lights, with a crooked number plate and wreaths on the front and the door.

He keeps a bright orange hose with a green tinsel garland running from the camper to the street grate. Now and then he empties the tank (steam, flies, a gurgle, and a neighbour groaning in Norwegian). A frizzy cat sits on a dumped armchair beside the bin bags.
Talk to him with E (or tap) to hold the hose: aim the stream at the grate while the pressure surges. Clean runs earn a title; afterwards he is, somehow, short of cash again.

He also challenges you to a chugging contest. Beer fills a small hidden-until-needed drunk meter: the world sways, you weave, and at the top you wake up beside his camper. Drunk driving gets the police interested.

entries.title: Laser tag arena: smoke
items: The Banken Arena now has a haze of fog-machine smoke. It is thicker in some lanes and thin in others, drifts slowly so it keeps changing, and now and then a floor vent puffs out a big dense cloud. The neon and the blacklight catch in it.
You see a little less far, so sneaking works, but you can still read the arena, the HUD and the enemy vests. Bots and tag hits are unchanged.
Weaker PCs get fewer smoke puffs, the weakest only a light haze, and it switches itself off if the game starts to lag.

entries.title: Snowball arena trash-talk
items: The snowball arena bots now shout 43 over-the-top one-liners: when they hit someone, when they get hit, when they dig in behind a wall or in a cave, when they run out of snowballs and when their team wins a round. Several different voices, and every bot has a couple of favourite lines.
You hear them from where they stand, only when you are close enough, quieter under the thwacks and whistles. Nobody talks non-stop and a line never repeats within a minute.
The arena announcer now also says a few extra lines at the start, in the middle of a match and now and then (including one about the Frost Troll). Weaker phones and PCs get fewer lines.

entries.title: Laser tag bots trash-talk
items: The laser tag bots (and the second player's stand-in) now shout over-the-top action-game one-liners: when they tag you, when they get tagged, when they hide in the smoke, and in the last 30 seconds. Different voices for the blue and red teams, and each bot has its favourite lines.
You hear them from where they stand, quieter when they are far away or when the shooting is loud. Nobody talks non-stop.
The referee has new lines too: a welcome, a one-minute warning, safety reminders, and a closing line for both winner and loser.

entries.title: Laser tag has a proper soundtrack
items: Banken Arena now plays a hard, driving electronic rock track while you play: "Harmful or Fatal" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com, CC BY 4.0).
It runs about five and a half minutes before it loops, and the arena lights still pulse with the bass.

entries.title: The course now sounds like a real live event
items: The two commentators now boom out of a stadium loudspeaker, with echoes rolling back off the hills, and they sit level with the music.
You can hear the whole show from far away: first a faint, muffled murmur and booming voices carried on the wind from about two kilometres out, getting clearer and louder as you walk closer.

They call the action for every other runner too: eight local competitors take turns on the course, with introductions, obstacle call-outs, wobbles, falls, finishes, and the crowd reacting. They also comment on your ghost run.
The crowd now really cheers, claps and groans when something happens on the course.

entries.title: Richer, filmier winter look
items: Colours now roll off to white like film instead of clipping, so lamps and snow look richer.
A low winter haze lies over the town with warm glows around the street lamps, and the snow twinkles near the lamps. Roads shine like ice.
Only on strong and good computers; slower computers keep the old look and run just as fast.

entries.title: Smoother opening flight, no more ice loading in
items: The ice no longer builds up along the river while the opening flight plays: the river is just the dark water, and out in the game the ice now fades in gently around you instead of ending in a hard edge.
The opening flight runs smoother: no more long freezes when the town comes into view, and less work for slower computers.

entries.title: Car headlights that really light the road
items: The odd see-through cone in front of the car is gone. Headlights now light the road, the verges and the people ahead of you at night.
Press F in a car for the high beam: it reaches about twice as far (D-pad right on a controller).
Brake lights glow brighter when you brake, and white reverse lights come on when you back up.
In snow and fog you can see a faint beam in the air. Other cars throw a soft light on the road in front of them.
Weak computers get the same lit road using a cheap glow on the ground.

entries.title: More street lights
items: About 575 new street lamps along roads through the populated valley, including the main road
Lamps stand 1.3 m off the road, every 35 m, and the Ninja plateau stays dark

entries.title: The ninja course walls are solid now
items: The warped wall and the Mega Wall were see-through from above; they are now solid blocks with stripes, and every other part of the course was checked the same way.

entries.title: Music app in your phone: pick the music yourself
items: Open the phone and choose Music (next to GPS). Albums are the radio stations (Downtown FM, Jazzy Jul, Kor & Kirke, Klassisk Jul, Nattevakt) plus the game music, all real recordings. Play, pause, next, previous, shuffle, repeat and its own volume, and the phone remembers your last track.

While it plays, the town music steps aside and comes back when you stop. It pauses by itself in the cinema, laser tag, the arenas, the Ninja Warrior course and cutscenes, and stops when the phone is switched OFF. Closing the flip lid keeps the music going: the closed phone shows the track name.
The Settings sliders, the M key and the car radio work exactly as before.

entries.title: The ninja commentators take centre stage
items: Ninja course sound: Brock and Tank are now the loudest and clearest thing you hear. When they talk, the music, the crowd and the wind step aside smoothly, and every voice line has the same loudness.
The crowd swells at the finish and at records without drowning the commentators. The course has a slot for a Christmas run anthem that starts on the countdown and fades when you leave.

entries.title: Still water is silent now: only rivers and rapids make water sounds
items: Lakes, ponds, the Ninja Warrior pool and the lake plateau, the fjord shore and the skating rink no longer trickle. Only moving water (rivers, streams, rapids) plays the water sound, louder near rapids.

entries.title: NAF Veihjelp is always in your phone: stuck? Call for roadside help
items: NAF Veihjelp is now the top Contacts entry all the time, also in the main phone menu (NAF 02016) and by typing 02016 on the keys. Menu: Stuck (pull me out), Wrecked (tow), Out of fuel, Won't start (jump start), Find my car.

Stuck on a snow bank, in a ditch, flipped, or pressing the throttle and going nowhere for 6 seconds: a message asks 'You seem stuck. Call NAF Veihjelp?' Press J (or tap the button) and a yellow truck drives in and winches your car back onto the road, nose along the road.
The price is shown first: pull-out 350 kr, more at night and far from town. No money? 'We do payment plans': the truck comes and you pay on your next call.
The operator talks (subtitles on). Stolen car while the police are after you: NAF says no. Never stuck for good: after 60 seconds you are offered a free lift to the nearest road (J).
Press J any time to open the NAF menu in the phone.

entries.title: DERPMAX cinema: both doors lead to the tickets, big TICKETS sign, no more books
items: The old library door in the Kulturhus (right under the big DERPMAX billboard) used to open into the bookshop. It now leads into the DERPMAX lobby, just like the red-carpet door; the Kulturhus has no separate library any more.
A neon DERPMAX signpost with arrows to both doors stands on the pavement, the second door has its own TICKETS sign, gold frame and carpet.

Inside the lobby: a big glowing TICKETS arrow sign, a hint at the top (TICKETS: the booth is on your LEFT), a one-time pop-up the first time you visit, and you now enter facing the booth. The booth is on the left, and the welcome and usher lines say so.
Pressing G in the cinema lobby can no longer open a shop. On the map and GPS, Kino, Kulturhus and the old library are now one DERPMAX marker at the cinema door.

entries.title: Smoother on slow computers: no more graphics flapping, chunk builds in slices
items: The automatic lag guard no longer flips back and forth (the shadow flapping): going back up now needs 30 seconds of calm, doubling each time it fails, and shadows, bloom, view distance and picture size each have their own minimum wait.

When the game runs slowly it now also thins out weather particles, refreshes shadows less often, updates far villagers less often, lowers the cinema video rate and shrinks the Ninja Warrior crowd, step by step.

Building a new piece of town used to freeze the game for one long moment on slow computers; it is now done in small slices over several frames. Clicking the lag pop-up (one click = one graphics level lower) still works and the guard starts fresh after it.

entries.title: Fewer draw calls on weak PCs
items: Behind the scenes, only on the LOW and POTATO graphics levels: people and cars far away are now drawn as one simple shape each (they switch back to full detail when you get closer).

On every graphics level: bridge and deck pieces far away are no longer drawn (they used to be drawn even kilometres away) and the rest are merged into fewer pieces. This takes the town square on POTATO from 863 to about 485 draw calls and Chris's house from 748 to about 550. Nothing changes visually.

entries.title: Homes: every room reachable, nothing cut off
items: Homes are planned so the kitchen, bathroom, bed and TV can always be walked to from the front door: nothing is placed if it would cut a room off. In the real-collision check of all homes, 77% now pass every test (was 23%) and only 4% have anything unreachable (was 24%).

Front doors that opened onto a solid wall, stairs that blocked the way, and bathrooms right behind the front door are fixed. Small homes get the essentials first (bed, stove, fridge, sink, wood stove, a seat) and less clutter. An armchair now counts as a seat.
Thin dark lines on the diagonal walls of rotated homes are gone. Homes plan faster, so walking through town hitches less.

entries.title: Old coins and the money changer on the square
items: New: old fantasy coins you can find, an OREN (gold), a FLOREN (silver), and two rare collector coins, the OLD KING'S KRONE and the TROLL PENNY. They are real items with little pixel icons, they stack, and the wallet in the corner counts them next to your kroner.
Shops, stalls, buses, garages and house sellers do NOT take them. Try it and the shopkeeper has something to say about it.

Only a money changer turns them into kroner: the VEKSLINGSKONTOR (Bureau de Change) is a small booth on the square by the town hall, run by a man in a very tall hat. The exchange screen shows today's rate, a funny market ticker, a chart of the last 7 days and buttons to change one or all. He pays a bit less than the market rate, takes a small fee, and pays out at most 3 000 kr a day. The rate drifts from day to day. After dark he goes home, and a shady man with a lantern turns up by the graveyard instead, with a worse rate and no questions.

Rare coins sell for far more than a normal coin, and the changer is collecting them for his Museum of Old Coins: a glass case on his counter that fills up. Bring him five and you get a reward and a better rate for good.

Where to find them: chests and crates (a small chance in every one), more on the summits, in boathouses and deep in the troll caves (cave 2 and cave 3 are the richest), as a tip for good jobs and deliveries, and very rarely lying on the ground. The rare ones only hide in the most dangerous old chests. They are a treasure, not a flood.

entries.title: DERPMAX: the cinema with an IMAX-style screen
items: The Kvinesdal Kino (in the Kulturhus) is now DERPMAX: a glowing neon door on the street side, a billboard and two poster cases outside. Walk in through the door.
Lobby: ticket booth (85 kr), a Now Showing board that changes by game day, a snack bar, eight pixel-art posters, an arcade corner, staff and a queue. The usher checks your ticket.

Auditorium: a 28 m curved screen with a glowing frame, 266 red velvet seats on steps, aisle lights, curtains that open, a projector beam with dust and a Kenney audience that laughs, gasps, claps and eats popcorn.
Sit with E: the lights dim, a Derp Studios card asks you to silence your phone (your phone really goes on silent), then the film plays. Hold Right to fast-forward, double-tap Right to skip.
Films: Marius's own videos (The Doors teaser, Meteor Night, The Round, Neon Round, Fly-In). New films: one file in data/cinema_programme.json (build/cinema/HOWTO_ADD_FILM.md).
New food items: Derp Popcorn (4 bites), Derpcola and Derp Candy, real inventory items.
Low graphics: a poster slideshow with the film's sound only.

entries.title: Something big out in the dark (venue, road and parking)
items: A huge lit-up rig with grandstands, a crowd, LED screens and a steaming pool has appeared somewhere out in the dark. A plain road leads most of the way there; cars are already parked, and tracks in the snow show where the spectators walked.
The big timer screen counts your run for real and remembers the best times of Chris and Martin.
Lykta spots the lights the first time you see them, and the phone GPS only learns the place after that (or when you get close).

entries.title: The Ninja Warrior course: run it yourself
items: Twelve huge obstacles to run: warped wall, floating steps, devil steps, spinning logs, salmon ladder, giant pendulum, cargo net, rope swing, balance beams, spinning bridge, slider and the Mega Wall.

You run it in first person with your own arms and legs (or third person with V). Build speed with Shift, jump, vault, grab ledges, hang, pull up, swing and climb. Your GRIP meter drains while you hang and refills on the ground.

Fall in the pool and you pop up at your last checkpoint. No damage, ever. 3-2-1 start, a big timer, 8 checkpoints, your best time, a ghost of your best run, and a sign with the best times of Chris and Martin.
Runner vision paints the next grips in neon red and orange. It fades after you have finished three runs; N turns it on and off.
Keys on the course: W A S D, Shift, Space (jump, grab, kip), E (countdown, kip, let go), Backspace (last checkpoint, Shift+Backspace restarts), Esc (leave).
Phone controls work on the course (stick, JUMP, USE, DOWN), the grips and the ladder beat are more forgiving, and the sounds are real recordings.

entries.title: Strange lights in the night sky
items: After dark, if you look far out over the dark land, you may see long beams sweeping up into the sky, with a glow under them. Walk toward them and a low thump and a crowd murmur slowly fade in.
Up close there are moving spotlights that sweep, cross and flash in colour, flame jets and fireworks on big moments.

entries.title: A secret ninja warrior course: commentators, news and gossip
items: Secret ninja course: two fictional American commentators (Brock Hollister and Tank Mulligan) shout about every obstacle, fall and finish, with subtitles, a lower-third banner and a volume slider in Settings.
From day 3 the TV news, Radio Kvina, Downtown FM, Heksa FM and the townspeople start talking about the strange lights in the sky and a secret ninja warrior course. Nobody says where it is.

entries.title: Snowball Arena: new gate on the Stadionvegen side
items: The arena gate is now in the long wall that faces the road and the stands (the river is on the other side, which has no gate any more). It sits past the end of the grandstand, nearest to Stadionvegen, with a glowing neon SNØBALLARENA gateway, lamp posts, a short lit path with a stepped ramp down to the footway, and you can walk straight in from the road.
Leaving through the gate puts you on that path facing the road, away from the arena. The phone GPS and map now take you to the gate, and people in town never stop or chat in the gateway.

entries.title: Lighter bridges and a gate report
items: Behind the scenes: the performance check was comparing against an old measurement taken at a lower graphics level, so it looked like the game had grown. It had not. Bridge and deck meshes now draw in fewer, bigger pieces (a few percent fewer draw calls everywhere, nothing changes visually).

entries.title: Laser tag at Banken Arena
items: Banken Arena (the sports hall by the stadium) is now a neon laser tag arena with two floors. Walk in through the glowing door on the south-east end (look for the BANKEN ARENA - LASER TAG sign). It shows on the map and phone GPS as 'Banken Arena · Laser tag'.

Inside: a lobby with a vest and gun desk, gun racks, lockers, a briefing room with the rules, an arcade corner, a snack bar, a scoreboard wall, an attendant and guests. Walk through the neon gate to start.

The arena has a ground floor and an upper floor around a big open middle, ramps, two bridges, a glowing central tower, mazes and cover, a blue base and a red base, and power pads upstairs (cyan shield, yellow rapid fire).

Your laser gun never runs out of shots. Hold fire and it overheats for a second. A hit lights the target's vest and tags them for 3 seconds. Rounds are 3 minutes: Chris (blue) vs Martin (red), or free-for-all against bots when you are alone. Winner ceremony with neon confetti, then rematch.

Dark blacklight look with pulsing neon, fog-machine haze and light shafts. The town stops updating while you are inside, so it runs lighter than outside. Lower graphics levels get fewer glow layers and fewer bots.

entries.title: Snowball Arena: the whole pitch, towers, caves and piles everywhere
items: The arena now covers the ENTIRE grass football pitch (104 by 68 metres, turned the same way as the real pitch) and stops at the pitch line: the running track around it is left alone. The gate is in the wall on the stand side.

Ten lookout towers with stairs and parapets (some with roofs and a passage underneath), a bridge between the two middle towers over a central snow hill with a tunnel through it, four igloos with two doors, two ice tunnels, a frozen pond that is slippery, snow forts, ramps, plateaus, pillars, low and tall walls and snowdrifts.

More than 50 glowing snowball piles all over the field (also on tower tops and inside the igloos). Hold G near a pile: 5 snowballs. Hold G anywhere on the snow: one snowball every 1.2 seconds, and with 0 to 2 left you slowly get one back every 6 seconds. The ammo counter is big and flashes red at zero, and an arrow points to the nearest pile when you are low.

You can no longer get turned around: the BLUE end wall and the RED end wall are painted in their colour with huge labels, flags on every tower, a BLUE END / RED END compass at the top, a small radar map with towers, piles and everybody on it, and you always start facing the enemy end. Walking out of the gate now turns you away from the arena (before, you came out facing into it).

Bots: 3 to 4 on each team when you play alone, they find their way round the walls, refill at the piles and climb towers and caves. Chris and Martin together play each other with bots filling empty places.

entries.title: Lights glow much further away
items: New slider in Settings > Look > Lights: Light radius. It sets how far away street lamps, torches and lit windows glow at night. The default is 100 m, much further than before; you can pick 30 to 400 m (a slower graphics level limits the top end) and reset it any time.
Far lamps now have a soft glow and a pool of light on the snow, so they no longer look switched off just 30 metres away. The glow fades in gently at the edge instead of popping on.
It is saved for each player, works on phones too (up to 150 m) and shortens itself automatically if the game starts to lag.

entries.title: Snowball Arena at the stadium
items: The football stadium (Kvinesdal stadion) has a walled snowball field with a gate, four lookout towers with stairs, snow forts, cover walls, flags, floodlights and scoreboards. Walk in through the gate to play: the town disappears and appears only as a very blurry picture around the field, and the game runs much lighter inside (about 5 ms a frame against about 12 ms in town in the first test).

Chris is blue, Martin is red: first to 10 hits or 3 minutes a round, best of 3, 10 snowballs, refill at the snow piles (hold G). A hit only freezes the other player in ice for a moment, no hearts are lost. A little nisse referee comments with a whistle and a voice.
Alone in the arena you play against 1 to 3 bots. It is also in the phone GPS and the map as Snøballarena. First draft: two-player sync is built but not yet tested between two real computers.

entries.title: Dev builder: statue grab fix
items: Clicking the bronze statue, a snowman or the Amot Bil sign in the builder now always grabs it, even when small snow decor is in front, so R turns it. A short message says 'Grab and spin is on' when the builder opens.

entries.title: Nobody stands in the road
items: Carollers now stop to sing on the pavement, never in the middle of the street, and walk along the kerb.
Townspeople no longer stop or chat in the road; anyone caught standing there steps aside with a 'Hey!'.
Cars stop and honk for anybody in their lane instead of creeping into them, and after a few seconds the person moves to the pavement.

entries.title: Dev builder: grab, move and spin everything
items: Everything you can grab in developer mode can now be moved and turned with R (15 degrees, Shift+R 90, Alt+R 1 degree, or the mouse wheel). The angle shows at the top of the screen.

The bronze statue, the 20 snowmen, the Amot Bil sign and the roadside board can be grabbed too: click, then M or drag to move, R to turn, Del to go back to how the code placed it. Your spot is saved with your other builder edits.
Trees, lamps and benches from the world turn into movable objects as soon as you press R.
The bronze statue is now real bronze: warm brown with a golden sheen, each of the four people a slightly different brown, and it now faces the other way. Turn it with R if you want it differently.

entries.title: Homes: nothing cut off, cosier rooms
items: If a fridge, stove, toilet, shower or bed was walled in by furniture, it is moved to a spot you can actually reach. Sofas, TVs, kitchen units and bathroom fixtures that got squeezed out are put back, and tables get chairs.
Entrance halls stay clear: no counters or cupboards in the passage behind the front door any more.
New: a folded wool blanket on sofas and at the foot of beds.
The little wall radio now plays a quiet Downtown FM song when you stand within 6 m of it (one radio at a time, silent when the car radio is on).
More radios, clocks, coat hooks, shoe racks and Christmas decorations in small and crooked houses.

entries.title: Homes make sense now
items: Every house was checked: the front door now opens into a proper hall, living room or kitchen (never a bathroom or bedroom), small homes get a bathroom and a bed, and every home gets a door mat, a radio on the wall and a clock.
Coat hooks and a shoe rack by the door in far more homes, wood stoves in the living rooms, a wood pile in cabins and farms and a tool corner on farms.
Furniture that blocked the way to a fridge, stove, toilet or door is left out, and pictures that hung in thin air are gone.

entries.title: The workshop is at Åmot Bil
items: The public car workshop (VERKSTED) has moved to where it is in real life: Åmot Bil AS on Industrigata at Åmot. It is a real garage now, with a roller door that opens by itself when you drive up and closes behind you, a car lift, a tool wall and a workbench.

You drive the car in, park it and press I. The workshop only works on THAT car: yours, Martin's camper van, a borrowed car, whichever you came in with. No more list of every car in town. On foot with no car it says 'drive a car in to work on it'.

The menu shows the car, who it belongs to, its health and upgrades, and there is a REPAIR button now (20 % dearer than at your own garage). Search 'verksted' in the phone or map to get a route to Åmot Bil. Your own garages work as before.

entries.title: The bronze statue by the bridge
items: At the east end of the footbridge by the river there is now a bronze statue: a woman in a long old-fashioned dress, two men and a small boy with a backpack, standing close together and looking out over the river. They are made of the same Kenney people as the rest of the town, but dark green-brown bronze, with snow on their heads and shoulders, on a rough granite plinth with a little plaque and four flower beds where the petunias are dead under the snow.
You cannot walk through it. It is on the map, in the search box and in the phone GPS as 'Bronsestatuen ved brua'.
At night, if you look at it from a bit away and then look somewhere else, the boy's head may be turned a little when you look back. Only once per night, and never when you stand close.

entries.title: People talk on the phone
items: When you call somebody on the phone, you now hear them talk. Fru Olsen, Herr Berg, Mamma, Tora, Gunnar, Kari and the others each have their own voice, and it is the same voice you hear in town.
The emergency numbers (112, 110, 113), the taxi, the pizza place, the speaking clock, the weather and the radio line answer with a voice too. Wrong numbers have strange voices.
It sounds like a real phone: thin and a bit tinny, right in the middle of your head. Nothing is heard when the phone is on SILENT or OFF, or when the flip phone is closed. Texts stay quiet.

entries.title: Hats for the snowmen
items: New side quest: twenty snowmen around town have no hats. Fru Ragnhild at the knitting stall (Strikk og lusekofter) has a box of twenty different hats: top hat, bobble hat, chef hat, crown, pot, bucket, colander and more.

Press G at a hatless snowman to put a hat on it. Each one has something to say, and a few are a little strange. Find them in the centre, at the school, the church, the ice rink, the bus stops, the cemetery and out on the hills.
Rewards from Fru Ragnhild at 5, 10 and 20 hats: money, red mittens and a snowman scarf. Progress is saved and shows in the quest journal (Q).

entries.title: People say it out loud
items: Townspeople, shopkeepers, market vendors, the video-lounge clerk and audience, kids and snowball fighters, officers and the Threshold whisperers now speak their bubble lines out loud (Norwegian or English as written), in 3D from where they stand.

Every person keeps the same voice: old, adult or young man or woman, kids have kid voices, officers have officer voices. Voices are only loaded when someone within about 14 m speaks, at most two at once (one on slow tiers).
The speech bubble stays up as long as the voice lasts. Nothing plays over cutscenes, story dialogue or phone calls, and the voice and sound sliders and indoor muffling apply as before.

entries.title: Your choices come back to you
items: New: the town now remembers what you do, and it comes back later, never straight away. Each time it lands it tells you why ("Because you ...").
Take a car and people see you: the shops nearby will not serve you until you pay for the damage (the bank always stays open). Hit someone and the police keep a record, so an arrest costs more.

Feed animals and they leave you a coin when you come back. Help someone with a quest and they send a thank-you the next day. If you dent a car and nobody sees, a note turns up asking for money. Paying or not is up to you.
Lykta comments on it in her amber text. A new TOWN tab in the quest journal, "What the town thinks of you", shows what people remember, in words, never as a score. Each player has their own.
Pay back what you borrowed from a neighbour (a plate of cookies is best) and they may drop by later with a small thank-you. Forget it, or ring 112 for nothing, and the town notices that too.

entries.title: The guide now shows how the game grew, in pictures
items: New guide section "How it grew: from the first block to today": a same-spot strip of the town square from the first versions to today, a gallery of milestone pictures with dates, and then-and-now pairs. The earliest picture is from 16 October.
Dates marked "about" come from when the picture file was saved. The player edition leaves out pictures that give away secrets.
New tool build/history_add.py lets us drop a new milestone screenshot into the history with a date and a caption.

entries.title: Your phone is social: text and call the town, borrow sugar for cookies
items: Contacts are real people with routines: Fru Olsen and Herr Berg next door from the start, the baker, kiosk, cafe, florist and shop owners once you meet them. They sleep at night, work in opening hours and go to church on Sundays

Text them from a menu (Borrow, Ask for help, Chat, Where are you, Are you open, Come over, Thanks / Sorry) or type your own. Replies come after a while, with Delivered, Read and typing... lines, and depend on the time, their mood and what you did to them

Out of sugar? Borrow sugar, flour, eggs, butter, milk, yeast, cocoa, spice, syrup, chocolate, tea lights, lantern oil or batteries. A paper bag shows up on your steps (or you come by the shop). You owe it back: bring the item, kroner, or best of all a plate of home-baked cookies for friendship and a good name

Calls work: neighbours pick up or take a voicemail, Mamma rings you and sometimes posts cookies, 112 / 110 / 113 (false alarms cost a fine; a real 113 sends an ambulance), taxi 07000, pizza and grocery delivery to your door, the speaking clock, the weather and the radio request line
Small extras: favourites, a missed-calls list, a gentle phone battery (charge at home or in a shop), autocorrect gags and the odd text from an unknown number at night

entries.title: Meteor day opener v2: on the frozen river, crater on the mountainside
items: CHANGED (draft): the people who spot the meteor now stand on the thick ice of the frozen river, so no building blocks the view: townspeople and skaters (the new Kenney people) look up at the sky, the loudspeaker pole stands on the ice, and you see the aurora, the stars and Nonskarknuten.

CHANGED: the crater is now on the town-facing SIDE of Nonskarknuten (about 300 m up, 60 % of the mountain), not on the summit ridge. A dark rim, burnt trees round it, a tall light beam and a red glow that you can see from the river ice. The quest 'Drive up to the crater' and its map marker point there; the track on the plateau runs about 100 m above it.

FIXED: keys pressed in the first seconds of the opener (while its sounds load) now count: Esc, fast-forward, double Space. A clicked PLAY button no longer eats the first key. Other game captions no longer show through the opener.

entries.title: No fog or snow inside buildings
items: Inside any house, shop, church, hospital, garage or the bowling hall the room is now clear: no fog, mist, snow flakes or northern lights, even in a blizzard or on a horror night. It fades back in smoothly when you step outside
The wind sound is also muffled indoors. Caves keep their own dark air, and the bowling hall keeps its bright light

entries.title: Christmas candles only in real windows
items: The little Christmas candle arches and paper stars no longer float on plain walls or house corners: they now sit only inside windows that really exist (candles on the sill, stars in tall windows, one per window)
Checked at night in 4 streets: 0 of 2352 decorations off a window (before: 6803 of 8574). Chunks also build no slower

entries.title: The barn at Valløyna has an opinion
items: Walk into the barn at Valløyna and look at the pile in the middle: your character says something out loud (and as a thought line) about whose work it is. 8 different lines, each in Chris's or Martin's own voice; always the first time, and now and then on later visits
New 'player quips' table (data/player_quips.json): any place can get its own funny comment, with a radius, a look-toward angle and a repeat chance

entries.title: The phone's Places is now a real GPS
items: The phone's Places app is renamed GPS (menu number 5). Pick a place and the phone closes, but the GPS stays on
A yellow route line follows the streets on the minimap and the big map, and on the ground in front of you (on medium graphics and up)
A strip at the top shows the next turn with the street name, the distance left and the time, with an arrow that points the way
A soft ding before each turn and a chime when you arrive; the GPS ends by itself. Left the route? It makes a new one
Cars and the bus get bigger turn text, and cars follow the one-way streets. Inside a building it first sends you to the door
The GPS list starts with Cancel GPS (while it is on), the Verksted, Home and Recent (your last five places)
Phone OFF turns the GPS off too, SILENT keeps it quiet; the strip hides during cutscenes

entries.title: Everyone is a Kenney person now
items: The ice skaters on the river rink (with skates; couples hold hands), the skier and the dog owner who shout "Hei!" and "Pelle!", the kids sledding by Liknes skole, the police officers and the drivers they pull out of cars, and the taxi passengers are now Kenney people too. No more odd box aliens. Nisser, trolls and the witch stay as they are, and so do you three.

entries.title: The phone is a flip phone
items: Open the phone and the closed flip phone rises up, then the lid swings open
Close it and you see the lid swing shut, hear a click, and it drops out of view
The little phone in the corner is a closed flip phone with a tiny window showing the time, a mail icon and a red dot for missed calls
When it rings, the closed phone wobbles: tap it to flip it open (the green key still answers)
New in Phone > Settings: 'Answer on open' and 'Keep call on close' (both off to start with)

entries.title: The guide is a real manual now (two editions)
items: The player guide grew from 51 to 95 pages: new chapters on day and night, the places table, the people of the town, your character and clothes, shops and money, the vehicles, the quests and favours, flying, Bowlinghallen, the animals and what they eat, the phone, maps and search, winter life, sound settings, troubleshooting and weak computers, credits and licences, and a Norwegian word list.
The guide has no story spoilers: secrets show as ??? (secret).

Marius gets his own edition (Downtown_Adventure_Guide_MARIUS.pdf) with the system-by-system overview, debug hooks, the 24-day table, the secrets list, the job queue, open decisions, the week digest and the known gaps.

entries.title: Lights you place in the builder now light up the room
items: Ceiling lights, pendant lamps, spots, table lamps, bedside lamps, floor lamps, candles, string lights, fireplaces and wood stoves placed in the builder now really light their room. Before, they only glowed and the room stayed dark.
Light is warm and cosy, white and brighter in shops, and stays inside the room it hangs in. Lights hung very high in tall shop halls still reach the floor.
On strong computers the nearest lights are real lights; on weaker ones a cheap room glow is used; on the weakest the room is simply brightened. Any number of lights can be placed without lag.

In the builder, a selected light shows a yellow ring (how far it reaches) and a blue box (the room it fills), and the inspector has LIGHT STRENGTH and LIGHT RANGE fields. Your saved builder objects are never changed unless you use those fields.

entries.title: Advent days list + the Meteor day opener (first draft)
items: NEW in Settings: a section 'Advent days (1-24)'. It lists all 24 days: which opener (cutscene or quick-time event) plays when you open that day's door, a green or grey dot, a PLAY button for the ones that exist, and a dropdown to pick which opener belongs to which day. Day 1 shows the intro flyover and the witch opening; the old scenes (banishment, the quick-time moments) are in the list too.

NEW (draft): METEOR DAY opener, about 90 seconds: the TV news promises a fun meteor night, the loudspeakers and the bell warn the town, you must spot the fireball in a quick-time event (3 key presses; missing never blocks you, it only changes the line), you ride the meteor down over the town, it hits Nonskarknuten with a flash and a shockwave, and a glowing crater stays on the mountainside. Then you get the quest: Drive up to the crater.

How to try it: Settings > Advent days (1-24) > Meteor day (draft) > PLAY, or add ?meteor=1 to the address. Hold or tap Right to fast-forward (4x, 8x, 16x), Left = normal, Space twice = +8 seconds, Esc skips. The day for it is not decided yet.

entries.title: The phone is a proper old Nokia now
items: The phone has real keys like an old Nokia: two soft keys under the screen, a round navigation key, a GREEN call key and a RED end key, and a number pad with letters under 2 to 9.
When someone rings, the green call key blinks and the screen says Answer. The phone never answers by itself: press the green key or Answer (or Enter on the keyboard). The red key or Decline says no.

The phone starts on a standby screen with the clock, the date, signal and battery, and tells you about new texts and missed calls. Menu opens the numbered menu, Names has a search where you type letters with the number keys like in the old days.

In a call there is a timer and Options (mute, speaker, hold). Hold the red key to switch the phone off, hold # for silent, hold * to lock the keys, hold 1 for voicemail. Type a number on standby and press the green key to call.
Snake still works with the navigation key, the arrow keys and 2, 4, 6, 8. Keyboard: Enter = green key, Backspace = back, C = red key.

entries.title: The phone can be silent or switched off
items: New phone ringer modes. ON is like before. SILENT never rings or pops up: the little phone in the bottom left corner just buzzes and shakes, shows how many texts you have not read, and glows green when someone calls. Tap it (or press P) to answer or read. If you miss a call it is written in the phone as Missed call.

OFF turns the phone completely off: no sound, no buzzing, the little phone goes grey. Calls and texts are saved, and when you turn it on again (tap the icon) it boots up and shows what you missed while it was off.
