Switch with Shift+P, in Phone > Settings > Ringer, by holding your finger on the phone icon (phones) or right-clicking it. The game is remembered between visits.

entries.title: Snow on POTATO is real snow now
items: On the lowest graphics level the snow used to be a flat picture stuck to the screen. Now the flakes fall in the world, drift with the wind, and slide past as you turn and walk, like on the other levels. It stays hidden indoors and follows the weather.

entries.title: Everything of note is on the map, in search and in the phone
items: New: hospital, police, fire station, schools, libraries, post offices, museums, culture house, the church, the bowling hall, the bandstand, the Christmas tree lot (Juletresalg), the market and its stalls, the ice rink (Skøytebane), gas stations, car repair, bus stops, and the VERKSTED workshop now show on the big map and in the search box, by Norwegian and English name (try: hospital, sykehus, politi, workshop, tree, skøyte, bus stop).

Places on the map follow where things really are: if the square, bandstand or tree lot is moved they move too. New map layers: PLACES & SERVICES, CARS & FUEL, BUS STOPS. Your own garages and car are listed too.

The phone has a new GPS app (menu number 5, first called Places): a search field, categories, and a live distance and arrow to each place. Pick one and the compass guides you there. The Verksted is always the first row.
Secrets stay secret: nothing undiscovered is listed (fast-travel lanterns only once found).

entries.title: Bowling alley sounds: balls, pins, gutters, cheers
items: Bowling now sounds like bowling, and it comes from the lane it happens on: the thud as the ball lands, the long rumble while it rolls, a hollow clatter in the gutter, the crash of the pins (a single tipping pin, a few, many, or a full strike), the pinsetter sweeping and setting new pins, and the ball rumbling back to the return. The other bowlers' games make the same sounds.
Reactions: a cheer and applause on a strike, a groan on a gutter ball, a murmur of approval on a spare, and the people say things: "Fin kule!", "Å nei, rennen!", "Strike!" (Norwegian and English).

The hall has a proper background: chatter, distant lanes, the neon and arcade, squeaking shoes and glasses clinking at the bar, plus small talk at the bar, the arcade and the lanes. It only plays inside, and only one person talks at a time, never over the story.

entries.title: The town square, your second plan
items: The town square now follows the plan you saved this morning: the Christmas tree lot (rotated, west of the square), the market stalls, Santa's sleigh, the benches, lamps, bins and street trees you moved, and the paper star. The ATV you removed is gone.

entries.title: Your clothes laid out on a paper doll
items: The WEARING boxes are bigger and sit where the clothes go on a person: hat above the head, face mask on the face, scarf at the neck, jacket and jumper on the chest, gloves at the hands, trousers, boots at the bottom.

The elytra (BACK) and the backpack (BAG) stand on the left as a back view. The warmth bar, KITCHEN, WRAP GIFT and the buttons are on the right, or under the doll in a narrow window, so nothing is cut off.
Clothes you wear also colour the little person. Click a box to take it off, same as before.

entries.title: The river freezes: skate on it, fall through the open water
items: Most of the river is frozen now (about 85 %): walk and drive on the white-blue ice, it is slippery
Dark open water stays under the bridges, in the fast stretches, in a few holes and in the fjord, with a cracked thin-ice edge as a warning
Fall in and you have 10 seconds before you freeze: swim to the ice edge and push forward or jump to climb out, or wake up at Kvinesdal legesenter for 300 kr
Cars sink in open water, and thin ice cracks and breaks under a car
Near town a cleared rink with a bench and a sign: kids, a couple holding hands and someone falling over go skating in the afternoon, evening and weekends

entries.title: Square layout tool: the Christmas tree lot is in it
items: The blueprint tool (square.html) now shows the Christmas tree lot (JULETRESALG) in both NOW and PLAN: drag it, rotate it, and see the seller hut and which side the entrance is on. When you save, the lot, its fence, trees, hut, seller and signs move in the game to where you put it.
The lot's default spot is a little smaller (15 x 10 m, centred north of the bandstand) so it no longer overlaps the market stall and the bandstand.

entries.title: Everything you buy lands in your inventory
items: Fixed: things bought at the stalls and shops could end up somewhere you could not see (worn without a message, or in invisible pockets). Now every purchase is a real item in your inventory, or it goes on you with a clear message such as "Put on: Red nisse hat (in your HAT slot)".
The shop window shows a note after each purchase, and how many places you have left in your backpack.
If your backpack is full, the shop says no and takes no money. And if anything you paid for ever fails to arrive, the money is paid back automatically.
Everyone now starts with Chris's old backpack on (36 places). The bigger packs are still for sale.

entries.title: Your phone, in your hand
items: A little phone button sits bottom-left: click it to pull the phone up (calls, texts, Snake, NAF)
The open phone is big and tilted in front of you, as if you are holding it

entries.title: Bowling hall: bright and cozy inside
items: Inside Bowlinghallen it is always lit like a clear 10:00 morning, day or night, and fades back to the real time when you step out
Warm glowing ceiling lights over the lanes, pin decks, carpet and bar; the 90s carpet and the wooden lanes show their colours

entries.title: A phone in your pocket: calls, texts, Snake and NAF
items: A little grey-blue 3310-style phone slides up in the corner when someone rings or texts: jobs, Mamma, the bank and the police. Press P for Messages, Contacts and Settings
Snake is in the Games menu (arrow keys or WASD, the keypad on touch), with a saved high score
Wrecked your car? Call NAF Veihjelp from Contacts: a yellow truck comes and fixes it for a fee (or tows it to your garage)

entries.title: The dark side of town
items: Rare, quiet dread at night and in fog (never a jump-scare, at most one every few minutes): a tall dark figure far down a street that is gone when you get close; a street lamp that flickers and dies as you pass; footsteps in the snow beside yours that are not yours; the car radio drifting into Heksa FM and a whisper; a phone ringing in a dark house; a grey villager in the Threshold who turns and watches you; and the church bell tolling once at 03:00.
Some nights a dense low fog rolls in off the fjord, shrinking the view until morning.

Eight clues are hidden around town (a missing-person poster, a torn notebook page, a spiral carved into three trees, a radio that hums, a ring where no snow settles, a school photograph with a child cut out). Press G beside one to read it; each goes into the NCC case file.
Settings > World life > "Spooky events: ON / LOW / OFF" turns the events down or off (the clues stay).

entries.title: Townspeople can walk everywhere
items: The walking network is joined up: 1,470 broken-off pieces are now 19, so people really walk to shops, work, school and home
Far fewer walkers teleport across town: almost every trip now has a real route
More houses and garages have a way to their door

entries.title: Lykta talks about what she sees, and the townspeople have voices
items: New: Lykta comments out loud (with subtitles) on what she sees: the square, the church, the troll caves, Feda, the fjord, the tree lot, the carolers, the witch's flat, a crash, the police chase, flying, opening a chest, finishing a quest, Mamma's letters and the bus. About 60 lines, never more than one comment every 45 seconds, never in a cutscene. Settings > Sound: LYKTA COMMENTS Chatty / Quiet / Off.

New: townspeople, shopkeepers and police officers now say their speech-bubble lines out loud in Norwegian and English (gossip about what you did, "Ring politiet!", the tree seller, "STOPP! POLITIET!"). You only hear them when you are close, one at a time, from the right direction.
All the text is in data/npc_lines.json; run build/make_npc_voices.py to make the voices again after editing.

entries.title: Sound polish: doors, wind, house noises
items: Doors never sound the same twice in a row: more variety and pitch from the real door recordings, and walking through an entrance no longer stacks a computer creak on the real one.
Wind now gusts: swells and dips, brighter and whistling higher up and in storms, calmer in the valley.
Indoors at night, rarely, the house settles: a beam creaks, a window sash squeaks and rattles in wind, a dull knock, a door closing far away, a sigh in the chimney (all from real recordings).
Footsteps vary a little more, and no clip repeats within two steps.

entries.title: Daily routines
items: People now follow the clock. On weekday mornings they leave home for work, shops and school; the shops fill up, lunch time sends people to the cafes, and in the afternoon they go shopping while the kids play after school.
In the evening people gather around the big tree and the market stalls, then go home and their windows light up. Late at night the streets are nearly empty.
Saturdays have no school and more strolling. Sundays are quiet, with church in the morning and a slow afternoon on the square.
A closed shop now says so at the door and on the shop screen: Stengt, åpner 09:00.

entries.title: Keys and the workshop
items: J now only opens the bauble list (Chris joining you moved to Shift+J).
The workshop (VERKSTED) screen fits on a phone held sideways, and the car speedometer no longer covers it.
The winged car lets the music know when it is flying.

entries.title: The music follows what you do
items: New: the music now changes with what is happening. A music-box tune indoors (muffled, cozy), a sad one at dusk, a spooky ambient piece at night and in the small hours, the creepy waltz when the police chase you, a happy polka in a snowball fight or a race, a deep choir drone in the troll caves, a cozy snow tune while you decorate the tree or read Mamma's letters.
It fades smoothly (2 to 4 seconds), never plays two songs at once, stays quiet when the car radio is on or carolers sing, and follows the M key and the music volume.

entries.title: Garage upgrade shop: wings, rockets and more
items: New: upgrade your cars at a garage you own (press I at the sign) or at the public VERKSTED workshop in town (20 % dearer). Wings (a real flying car: 40 km/h, then SPACE), rocket boosters (Z), snow chains, armour plating, a snowplough blade, Xmas lights, a carol horn (B) and paint.
Upgrades stay on the car, also when it is parked in your garage. The cat on the roof can now be rescued with a winged car.

entries.title: Letters and baubles polish
items: Mamma's letters: when your pockets are full the cookies wait in a bag at your feet, and the message now says so. On a phone the CLOSE button stays on screen while you read.
The NEW BAUBLE pop-up no longer covers the bauble list when it is open.

entries.title: Shopkeeper talk stays on screen
items: The little speech box above a shopkeeper (including the comment about your reputation and the prices) no longer gets cut off at the edge of the screen.

entries.title: Letters from Mamma
items: From day 7, Chris's mum writes real letters (nine of them, until day 23) that arrive in the mailbox, each with a batch of pepperkaker, a gingerbread house and some tea lights on the way.
Day 7 now opens Mamma's first letter, not a witch note. Mamma's letters are always read before the witch's notes.
Two letters were opened and eaten on the way: the cookies are fewer and the witch has scribbled at the bottom.
All her letters are kept in one item in the inventory, 'Mamma's letters'. Hold it and click, or USE: read.

entries.title: Buy a garage or a house
items: Five ordinary buildings now have a TIL SALGS / FOR SALE sign by the door: two garages and three houses. Press G at the sign to buy with the money you earn on the jobs board. The sign turns green (SOLGT).

A garage keeps your cars: park one inside, take it out again, repair it for a fee. A car you wreck or lose is towed back, damaged. A house is a bed that saves the game, with a box by the door for your presents.
Your garages (G), houses (H) and the ones for sale (S) show on the map.

entries.title: Decorating Chris's house
items: Chris's house starts bare after the witch's rampage: no tree in the yard, no lights, no stars, no wreath. Stand in the front yard and press G to decorate: stars in the top windows, lights on the roof, the windows, the path and the arch, and a wreath on the door.

Until 13 December the witch tears it all down about half a minute after you finish: you will hear her, see a green flash at her door, and watch the bulbs rip off and fall. From 13 December it all stays up.

entries.title: First quest: a tree for Chris
items: When the drive home from Feda is over, the first job is a Christmas tree. Buy one at the JULETRESALG on the square with the coins you picked up on the road (during this job the trees cost 240, 320 or 420 kr). Not enough? Lykta tells you how to earn the rest.
Get it home: drag it on foot (slow), put it on a car roof, or pay 40 kr extra to have it left at Chris's front step.

Chris lives upstairs: carry it up to the living room, press G on the glowing spot by the window to stand it up, then press G at the tree to decorate it. Mamma's old box of baubles, a star, lights and tinsel is waiting in your pockets.
The quest steps show a marker, a line on the screen and Lykta's lantern points the way. Chris and Martin share the same tree.

entries.title: Moon and planets in the sky
items: The moon and the planets now rise and set over the mountains: they sit far behind the ridges, never drawn in front of them, and are cut by the horizon so nothing floats below it.
Near the horizon they get dimmer and a little warmer, like in real air.
The moon phase now matches December 2026: new moon on 9 December, full moon on Christmas Eve.

entries.title: Subtitles and speech bubbles
items: When the police are after you, the thought and talk lines no longer cover the WANTED stars; they move up a little.
Speech bubbles over people wrap into a small box and stay on screen instead of running off the edge of a phone.

entries.title: Jobs from people in town
items: There is a cork board at the town square (press G beside it) with 15 short jobs: deliver buns, pizzas, a Christmas tree or medicine before the clock runs out (a crash can break the cargo), race for gold, silver and bronze, lose the police or Svarte-Kare, drive villagers around for tips, catch a runaway reindeer, rescue a cat from a roof and hunt gingerbread men.
People also phone you with jobs now and then. Press P to answer. You are paid in kroner and the town thinks better of you. Backspace gives a job up.

entries.title: Gentler steps at four shops
items: Apotek 1, Sofie's salong, Power and Extra had a full-block step at the door that needed a jump. Each now has a half-block step, so you just walk in and out.

entries.title: 23 baubles for the tree
items: There are 23 special baubles, one for every day of the advent. Some are rewards from people in town, some are in treasure chests, and some float in hard-to-reach places like summits, caves and a sky island.

Press J (or BAUBLES in the phone menu) to see your collection. Hang them on the Christmas tree from the decorating panel. The witch still tears the tree down before 13 Dec, but your baubles are never lost.
Found baubles show up on the big map.

entries.title: Beds save your game
items: Sleep in a bed that is yours (Chris's house, Martin's room in Chris's house, Marius's and Martin's homes, cabins) and the game is saved: where you are, your bag, your money and the time. You see a big SAVED message.
If the game restarts or crashes, you wake up next to the last bed you slept in.
Other people's beds still let you sleep, but they tell you nothing was saved.

entries.title: Garage doors and street signs
items: Garages, sheds and warehouses now have a door frame around their openings instead of a plain hole in the wall.
The LEGESENTER sign by the health centre shows the whole word again (it was cut off by the red cross).

entries.title: The town reacts to you
items: People now run away and scream when a car races at them, when there is a crash, when someone is hit, in a police chase, at a firework bang, or if a troll is out. Some hide behind the nearest door for a while, then everyone calms down.
Some neighbours phone the police ("Ring politiet!"): if they saw you do it, your wanted level goes up. Others hold up their phone with a red recording light and film you.
The films show up later as a reader video on TV channel 4 (Kvinesdal Nytt) and as a story on Radio Kvina.
People gossip about what you did when you walk past (it fades over about three game days). Shopkeepers talk about it too, and charge a little more if your name is bad.
Good deeds count: finishing quests and tipping the carol singers make the town friendlier, with waves and kind words. Children never film, never phone the police and are never in the gossip.

entries.title: Roads and signs
items: Øye: the petrol station's roof was built as a solid block right on top of the road; it is gone, so you can drive through again.
Shop signs (Nico Senter, EXTRA and the others) now sit against their wall instead of hanging out over the pavement.
Baking on a phone: all twelve cookies can be tapped in the cutting step.

entries.title: Things to do inside houses
items: In the furnished houses, press G at a lamp to switch the lights off and on, at a bed to sleep (at night you wake up at 07:00), at a fridge for a snack, and at the toilet, sink, shower, stove, fireplace, piano or washing machine.
The warm window glow and the walls go dark when the lights are off, so a night in a dark house feels different.

entries.title: Hospital and the police station
items: If you die (a fall, a crash, the cold) you now wake up at Kvinesdal legesenter, and the hospital bill is 300 kr. The witch, the Eye and the Hollow still send you somewhere safer, like before.
If the police catch you, the screen fades, you wake up at the lensmannskontor by the town hall, pay a 500 kr fine, and the stars are gone.

entries.title: Taking cars
items: Press G beside a car somebody is driving and you pull the driver out. He stumbles, shouts and runs off, and you drive away. Somebody saw it, so the police want you.
Parked cars are locked now. Press G to pick the lock (a small bar fills up), or let go and press G again to smash the window. Half the time the car alarm goes off.
Martin's van, the cars in Chris's lot, mopeds, ATVs and cars you have already driven are still free to hop into.

entries.title: Wanted level and the police
items: Hit or run over someone, ram cars or the police, and if anybody sees it you get stars (1 to 5) above your hearts. Hide out of sight and the stars slowly fade.
Norwegian police cars (white with the blue and yellow band, POLITI on the doors) chase you along the roads with blue lights and a low siren.
From 3 stars they set up a roadblock ahead of you. Officers jump out, shout STOPP! and run after you. If they get hold of you, you are arrested.

entries.title: Baking on the phone
items: The baking screen now fits on a phone held sideways: the instructions, the progress bar and the GIVE UP button are on screen while you stir and roll.
In the kitchen, the amounts next to each ingredient (0 / 1) stay on one line.

entries.title: World fixes: far areas checked
items: Went through Åmot, the edge of Liknes (incl. Liknes skole), Feda, Storekvina and the main road between them: all house and shop doors have open space in front and the road is clear all the way from Feda to Liknes and up to Storekvina.
Feda church and any other church now get the same big wooden double doors with an arch.

entries.title: Decorations, wrapped gifts and books
items: The Christmas decorations are real things now: baubles, the straw star, a string of lights that twinkle, tinsel, little nisser, candles, lanterns and flowers.

At a Christmas tree, press G to decorate it: hang baubles, put on the star, string the lights, wrap the tinsel. Until 13 December the witch tears it all down after a little while (everything comes back to your pockets). From 13 December it stays.
Hold a decoration and right-click to set it down; press G next to it to pick it up again.
Gifts: buy Gavepapir (wrapping paper), then WRAP GIFT in the inventory wraps any item for Chris, Martin or Mamma. Put presents under the tree; the one they are for can open them on Christmas Eve.
Books and the newspaper can be read: six little stories from the library, and a new headline in the Avis every day.

entries.title: Baking game: mix, roll, cut, and watch the oven
items: Baking is a little game now. On a baking card in the kitchen: stir the bowl, roll out the dough, cut the shapes, and put the tray in the oven.

Take the tray out in the green window and the food is PERFECT: golden, more hearts and warmth, nice as a gift. A bit early or late is fine. Too long and it BURNS: smoke fills the kitchen, the smoke alarm goes off and the whole batch is ruined (burnt food is still edible, one heart).
The ingredients are used up when you start, so a burnt batch means another trip to the shops.
Wearing the chef hat gives you a wider green window and a little more time.
The game counts your perfect, normal and burnt batches. The witch is very interested in your cookies.

entries.title: The kitchen: real ingredients and recipe cards
items: The shops now sell real baking ingredients: flour, sugar and eggs at Nico Mat, butter and yeast at the bakery, gingerbread spice at the Gløgg stall, syrup and chocolate at the candy stall, cocoa powder at the cafe.
Some days one shop is sold out of something. Another shop has it for a bit more, so a baking day can turn into a little shopping round.
The old 3x3 crafting grid is gone. Press G at the stove in Chris's kitchen: recipe cards show what you have, what is missing and which shop sells it.
Ten cards: pepperkaker, lussekatter, waffles, Grandiosa from the oven, a gingerbread house, hot cocoa, hot chocolate, home-made gløgg, a snow lantern and lantern oil.
Baked food comes in three kinds: perfect (more hearts and warmth, nice as a gift), normal, and burnt (only one heart).

entries.title: World fixes: proper church doors
items: Kvinesdal kirke now has big wooden double doors with iron straps and a round arch with a glowing fanlight above them. They swing open when you walk up, so you can still walk straight in.
The little picture in 'How to play on phone': the ITEM label now fits inside its box.

entries.title: World fixes: church front and sign text
items: Kvinesdal kirke no longer looks like a shop: no glowing shop sign and no glass shop front, just church windows and a doorway.
Shop sign text now shrinks to fit, so long names (like KVINESDAL KIRKE) are no longer cut off at the ends.

entries.title: Loot! 170 new chests and crates, coins on the ground
items: 170 new chests and crates are hidden around the world: behind the shops in town, behind sheds and barns, at boathouses, by cabins, deep in the forest, under a few bridges, near the troll cave mouths and up on the mountain tops. Crates are made of lighter wood. They show on the big map under TREASURE CHESTS, found or not found, like the old ones.

Better loot: almost every chest has money in it, from a few tens of kroner up to thousands in the rare ones on the summits. Many also hold flashlight batteries, food, clothes and hats, lantern oil, flares or a gløgg thermos, and now and then a backpack. When you have opened a chest, a short list shows everything you got.
The old chests that had not been opened yet use the new, better loot as well.
Small finds everywhere: coins lie on the ground in town and a bit rarer outside it, and some are hiding under the benches. Walk over them to pick them up. They come back after about 40 minutes.

entries.title: Clean-up: the old mining stuff is gone
items: The inventory is now only things that make sense in town: the armour sets, pickaxes, swords, ingots, raw ores, coal and gunpowder are gone, and breaking stone only gives you the stone block itself.
The crafting book is short now and useful: planks from a log, bricks from cobblestone, wool from string.
Old saves lose nothing: if you were carrying any of the old things, the game pays you kroner for them, and your first old axe turns into the Vedøks (the tree axe).
New games start with 32 planks, 64 snow, a Vedøks, 5 rockets, a flashlight and 3 batteries.
The CREATIVE button is only for the developer copy now. In the normal game everybody plays survival.

entries.title: Tools that make sense: axe, batteries, bell
items: Trees: you now need an axe to fell a tree. The Vedøks (axe) costs 149 kr at the hardware shop and one also lies on the square. Three swings, then "Timber!", and you get logs. With bare hands the game tells you what is missing.

Flashlight batteries: the flashlight no longer charges itself. One battery gives about 50 minutes of light. You start with 3. Hold a battery and click (or press L when the light is flat) to put a new one in. A small bar shows the percent and how many spare batteries you have, and the game warns you when it gets low. Batteries cost 89 kr at Elektronikk, the hardware shop and the fuel station, and they are in chests. Lamps, flares and the gløgg thermos still top it up.
Lantern oil (Lampeolje, 79 kr at the hardware shop and the fuel station): hold it and click to refill the lantern.
The sleigh bell rings when you click with it (left or right) using a real bell recording. The gløgg thermos now says what it does, and it warms you up too.
When you pick up a tool, a short line above the hotbar tells you what it does.

entries.title: The choir in the Threshold
items: In the Threshold world the carolers sing their song backwards, slowed and warbling, muffled as if through ice, with a deep echo
The bandstand choir can be heard across the whole square (and further) in the normal world

entries.title: Smoother town: no more stutter every few seconds
items: Fixed a small freeze that hit about every 3 seconds when walking around town (the game was re-checking its hidden-things list because sparks and smoke came and went).
Villagers walking the pavement make about 20% less memory garbage per frame, so fewer tiny pauses on slow computers.

entries.title: World fixes: invisible cars
items: Cars driving around town no longer go invisible on lower graphics levels. Before, MEDIUM, LOW and POTATO drew only some of the moving cars while the rest still drove, honked and could hit you. Now every moving car is always drawn.

entries.title: The game picks its graphics level and lets you step down in one click
items: First start: the game guesses a graphics level from your graphics card, memory and processor (never ULTRA; if it cannot tell, it starts on LOW). Anything you chose yourself is remembered and wins.

If the game runs slowly for about 5 seconds, a button appears: Game running slowly - click to lower graphics. One click goes down one level at once and you keep playing; if it is still slow later, it offers the next level, all the way to POTATO. The game never goes up by itself; after a long smooth spell it only offers one level up (never ULTRA). It stays quiet in the intro, cutscenes and the Threshold.
If the game closes badly twice within ten minutes on a PC, the next start is one level lower.

entries.title: Level caps: less building per frame on weaker levels
items: On MEDIUM, LOW and POTATO the game builds new town chunks in smaller slices (5, 4 and 3 ms per frame), so walking and driving stutter less on slow computers. HIGH is unchanged. People, animals and birds were already capped per level.

entries.title: Backpacks
items: Your pockets now hold 27 things. To carry more, buy a backpack: Skolesekk (249 kr, +9 places), Tursekk (599 kr, +18) or Fjellsekk (1 199 kr, +27, the biggest). The clothes and outdoor shop sells all three, Nico Mat sells the school bag, the hardware shop the two big ones.
A backpack has its own BAG place, so you can wear it together with the wings. You see the pack on your back in third person, and your friends see it online.
If you take a bag off and your things no longer fit, whatever does not fit is left in a small bag at your feet. Nothing is ever lost.
Old saves: if you had more than 27 things, the extra ones are tucked into free places or left in a bag at your feet.

entries.title: Hats, and friends see what you wear
items: Hats! Nisse hats in red, green, blue and white (small, medium and large: the big ones are tall and floppy), woolly beanies, bobble hats, ear-flap hats, caps, a top hat, reindeer antlers, a Lucia crown with little lights, a chef hat and a hard hat. They sit above your head and keep you a little warm.

Where: the Julepynt stall (nisse hats, antlers, Lucia crown), Strikk & ull (beanies, bobble hats, flap hats), the clothes shop (beanies, flap hats, caps, top hats), the bakery (chef hat) and the hardware shop (hard hat). Buy one for an empty HAT place and you put it on at once.
The golden nisse cap from the nisse trial is now a proper hat too.
When you play together online, your friends now see what you wear, hats included, and you see what they wear.
Old leather helmets from older saves turn into a red beanie.

entries.title: Shop signs you can see
items: The long dark canopy over the EXTRA door hung right at eye height and cut straight across the EXTRA sign, so it looked like a wall in front of the entrance. It now hangs high above the sign, with plenty of room to walk under.
Same for Nico Senter and the other shops with a glass canopy: their signs are readable again.
The flag poles in front of EXTRA no longer stand in the middle of the way to the door.
The graphics level buttons in Settings (ULTRA, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, POTATO) now fit their words on small screens.
Car radio: fixed a hidden fault that threw errors every moment while a station was playing (the volume and crossfade between stations could stop working).

entries.title: Clothes you can really wear
items: The old ARMOUR box is gone. The inventory now has ten places for what you wear: HAT, FACE, NECK, SWEATER, JACKET, LEGS, FEET, HANDS, BACK and BAG.
Clothes change how you look. Put on a jumper, a jacket, trousers, boots, mittens, a scarf or headphones and you see it on your character in third person (press VIEW).
Clothes keep you warm. The more you wear, the slower your warmth drops, and cold water chills you slower too. The inventory shows how much less chill you have.
The elytra (wings) now lives in BACK, so a jacket or a jumper never pushes it off. Wear both and fly.

Clothes are sold in the clothes shop (jumpers, jackets, trousers, boots, mittens, scarves), at the Strikk & ull stall (lusekofte, selbuvotter, socks) and headphones at the electronics shop. If you buy something for an empty place, you put it on straight away. Or hold it and right-click, or press WEAR in the inventory.
Old saves keep working: the leather things you wore turn into the matching real clothes.

entries.title: The Christmas tree lot
items: The tree seller now has a proper Christmas tree lot on the open snow near the bandstand: a fenced yard with string lights, rows of spruces in three sizes and a rack of netted ones, a seller hut with a JULETRESALG sign, an opening-hours board (09-21) and a price board. Talk to the seller to buy a tree.
Every market stall now has a keeper, including the ones you built yourself.

entries.title: Trash bins you can use
items: Every street bin and every wheelie bin by a house can now be used: stand next to it and press G (on a phone, tap the prompt). Your inventory opens with a TRASH slot. Pick up something you do not need, click TRASH and confirm, and it is gone for good. Things a quest still needs are refused.
Now and then there are a few kroner hiding in a bin (each bin only once in a while).
Bins are on the big map (new layer TRASH BINS) and on the small map when they are close. Press T and pick "Nearest trash bin" to teleport there or follow the guide.

When your pockets are full, buying is refused without taking your money, and the message says how far the nearest bin is. Lykta tells you where it is and points the way. Things you pick up that do not fit are left in a small bag at your feet; walk over it when you have room and it jumps back into your pockets.

entries.title: Shops give you real food
items: Everything you buy to eat or drink (sweets at Godteboden, Grandiosa, melk, brunost and appelsiner at Nico Mat, buns, coffee, pizza, pills ...) now goes into your inventory with its own little picture, instead of being eaten at the counter.
Hold it and click to take a bite (or press USE in the inventory). Your hunger bar and hearts go up, and hot drinks warm you. If you are already full, you are told so and nothing is used up.
If your pockets are full, the shop says so and keeps its hands off your money (bins to throw things away come later). Things you find that do not fit now wait for you instead of vanishing.

Rockets are gone from the grocery and the kiosk, and the shop lists lost a few silly lines (screwdriver, windscreen fluid, toothbrush, lip balm, PlayStation 2, parking permit, fishing licence, hair wax). Julekule and food you used to carry as "pockets" are now real items.

entries.title: Headlights that light the road
items: Your car now lights up the road, snow, walls and people ahead in the dark, with a soft beam you can see, and brake lights that glow red.
Traffic cars get a light pool on the road in front of them at night.

entries.title: Speedometer in every vehicle
items: A km/h readout with a little dial shows in the bottom right whenever you drive or ride anything. It turns red above 50 km/h.
In the first-person cockpit view the dashboard has a speed needle.

entries.title: Bail out of a moving car
items: Press G while the car is moving: the car keeps rolling with nobody in it, and can still crash into things and people.
Slow: you just step out. Fast: you dive out of the door, roll on the ground, and get up a bit hurt (the faster, the more).

entries.title: People are solid, and accidents happen
items: Walking into villagers now pushes them (and you); they stumble and complain.
Cars (yours and the traffic) knock people over at low speed. At higher speed it is a gruesome accident: the person is flung, stays down and bleeds, with blood on the road, the snow and the car.
New setting BLOOD: ON / OFF (Settings > World life). It is remembered. Children are only ever knocked over.

entries.title: Car crashes with real damage
items: Driving into walls, trees and other cars now bounces and spins the car, shakes the camera and crunches.
The car gets dented where it was hit, the lights go dark, the windows crack, and it smokes when it is badly hurt.
Hit hard enough, and the car is wrecked: it cannot drive any more. Press G to get out.

entries.title: Smoother driving camera
items: Steering with A and D now eases in and eases back to centre instead of snapping.
The chase camera follows the car smoothly, swings out in corners and looks a little ahead into the turn.

entries.title: Market life and the Christmas tree sale
items: Every market stall now has a keeper with their own goods on the counter (gløgg, knitwear, candles, roasted almonds, sausages, wooden toys, krumkaker). They open in the daytime and go home at night and on Sundays.

One stall is the JULETRESALG: rows of netted spruce trees in three sizes (450, 550 and 700 kr). Villagers buy a tree and drag it home behind them, and some cars drive around with a tree on the roof. You can buy one too, but it slows you down.

entries.title: The people of the Threshold, again
items: In the Threshold World every person is grey and faceless again, with the new Kenney bodies: villagers, shop staff, quest givers and strangers (the carolers and church choirs keep their own look, only their lanterns turn cold blue). They bow, stare at the sky or cower when you walk close, and the town stops its everyday life while it lasts.
The carolers and church choirs now sing like they are in the underworld: muffled, slow, low, drowned in echo, with a dark drone underneath.

entries.title: Ride the bus: line 12 to Feda and line 14 to Storekvina
items: Two bus lines now run on a real timetable every 2 hours: line 12 to Feda kai and line 14 to Storekvina. The times are printed on a sign at every stop.
Walk up to a waiting bus and press G (or tap) to pay the 45 kr fare, ride inside with the camera in the cabin, and press G at a stop to get off. Villagers wait, board and step off too.

entries.title: ULTRA and POTATO are real
items: ULTRA now uses the sharpest picture your screen has (up to twice the pixels), a bigger shadow map, one more ring of town drawn around you and far things stay visible longer. It is never chosen automatically.

POTATO is for very weak computers: the picture is drawn smaller and stretched up, there are no real shadows (soft dark spots under people, animals and cars instead), fewer people, 3 animals and 5 birds at most, the far view is covered in fog, snow is a flat falling-snow layer, and people far away move at 4 steps a second. Same town, same story.

LOW and MEDIUM got the same kind of numbers: smaller shadow map and fewer people on MEDIUM, no real shadows with soft spots instead, a shorter view and a slightly smaller picture on LOW. HIGH is unchanged.

entries.title: Lighter title screen and intro on weaker levels
items: The title screen, the flyover intro and the witch opening used to be the heaviest part of the game on every computer. Now they follow the graphics level: HIGH and ULTRA look exactly as before, MEDIUM builds a bit less of the valley ahead of time, LOW and POTATO build much less (far trees and the far valley are thinner, no extra-sharp picture while flying), same story and same flight.
Snow now follows the level too: fewer flakes on MEDIUM and LOW (a little bigger so it still looks snowy), and the shadows on MEDIUM refresh half as often. HIGH is unchanged.

entries.title: GTA-style car radio
items: Two new stations: Radio Kvina (104.3, local news, weather and traffic) and Nattevakt (97.7, late-night weird). Press R in a car to switch.
Every station has its own DJ now: Julius Jolly, Smooth Sverre, Sister Solveig, Maestro Magnus, Randi and Ole, Night Owl Nils. Heksa FM is still the witch.
DJs talk between songs and sometimes over the start of a song, and there are funny fake local ads (no real companies).
Radio Kvina reads the news on every game hour: the real time, the weather, the witch, the troll caves, accidents and the long drive to Feda change what you hear.
The radio shows a What's on line with the station DJ and what is playing (music, DJ, ad break, news).

entries.title: TV pictures sit on the screen, and 7 new channels
items: Fixed: the TV picture used to float in front of or beside the TV, tilted. It now sits exactly on the screen of every TV, at any angle
Press G at a TV with no tape to flip through 10 channels now; the prompt shows the channel names

New: 4 Kvinesdal Nytt (the real weather and time, plus a headline ticker), 5 Julekjøkkenet (cooking show), 6 Peiskos (crackling fireplace), 7 Snøstøy (static, and late at night something whispers), 8 Klosse og Kompis (voxel cartoon), 9 Julesalg-TV (shopping channel), 10 Trollhulen: Dokumentaren
TVs only redraw when you are close and looking at them, so they cost less

entries.title: Troll caves on the map and in search
items: Search for "troll" or "Trollhule" to jump to any troll cave (or use 🧭 GUIDE to walk there)
New TROLL CAVES layer on the big map shows every cave entrance

entries.title: Troll cave chests show their treasure
items: Opening a chest inside a troll cave now shows the little item scene (Martin holding the treasure up in a golden glow) like every other chest. Before, only the text box appeared and you saw nothing.
Less noise in the background: the game no longer asks for voice recordings that do not exist.

entries.title: Five graphics levels
items: Settings now has a GRAPHICS section with five levels: ULTRA, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW and POTATO. Your choice is remembered. HIGH is how the game looks today. (For now ULTRA looks like HIGH and POTATO like LOW; they get their own tricks soon.)

entries.title: Small fixes
items: Phone: the SENSE button (hold for the lantern sense) now sits by the JUMP button instead of hiding under the menu button
The settings panel says TIME AND WEATHER / CAMERA AND FILM (the & looked like a dollar sign)
The map credits line no longer hides behind the hotbar
The game loads a little faster on repeat visits

entries.title: No more frozen title screen when 3D cannot start
items: If a computer cannot start 3D (for example Edge with hardware acceleration switched off), the game now says so in plain words, tells you which switch to turn on in Chrome or Edge, and has a TRY AGAIN button, instead of sitting on a dead title menu.
The game tries gentler graphics settings by itself before it gives up, and if the picture is lost mid-game on a PC the message now makes sense for a computer.

entries.title: Troll caves
items: Two caves are cut into the hills: a rocky mouth with snow on top, ice crystals and two torches. Walk into the dark opening to go inside.
Inside there are winding tunnels, torches on the walls, bats flapping under the roof and big frost trolls that mumble and wander about. They only watch and grumble. Walk back to the light to leave.

entries.title: The town square, your plan
items: The Christmas tree, Santa's sleigh, the julekula, the market stalls and a snowman now stand where you placed them in the blueprint tool. The market keepers moved with their stalls, and the parked cars on the square are gone.

entries.title: Solid roads
items: Roads and pavements are now real solid blocks, with nothing hollow underneath. You no longer start the game under the road, and shop and house doorways are easy to walk into.

entries.title: Rubbish day
items: Wednesday is rubbish day. Wheelie bins go out to the kerb in the morning, an orange bin lorry drives round emptying them, and the bins go back in the afternoon.

entries.title: The bus keeps a timetable
items: The bus runs from 06 to 23 (09 to 20 on Sundays, with longer waits) and sleeps at night.
Villagers waiting at the stop get on, passengers get off, and each stop has a little sign showing the next departures.

entries.title: Gritted roads
items: Roads and pavements are now gritted. Grey grit speckles the ground, and ice patches only form where nobody has gritted. You slip and slide on the ice, but gritted ground grips.

entries.title: Chunky-cute town props
items: Benches, street lamps, bins, market stalls, the bandstand, Santa's sleigh, snowmen, nisser, camp tents and campfires, bus shelters, cairns, lanterns, mailboxes and prams have all been remade in the chunky-cute style. They stand in the same places and are just as solid.

entries.title: The morning post
items: A postman with a red bag walks the pavements, and a red Posten van stops with its hazard lights on.
Newspapers lie on doorsteps early in the morning, and a delivery truck unloads at the grocery. No post on Sundays.

entries.title: A smoother sky, and the tree moves
items: The stars, moon, planets, clouds and sun now glide smoothly across the sky instead of ticking along.
The town square's Christmas tree has moved to the true centre of the square, by the sleigh and the benches.

entries.title: Engine heaters
items: Some parked cars are plugged into the house with an engine-heater cable, and cars puff exhaust smoke when they start on cold mornings.

entries.title: Steaming breath and frosty cars
items: Your breath and the villagers' breath steams in the cold air. Parked cars get frosted windows on cold mornings, and now and then someone scrapes a windscreen.

entries.title: Echoes and muffled snow
items: Your footsteps echo indoors and boom in tunnels and churches, and a heavy snowstorm or thick fog muffles all the sound.

entries.title: Hunger and warmth (optional)
items: A tiny badge above the hearts slowly drifts as you get hungry or cold. A pølse, a gløgg or a warm fire fixes it.
It's never deadly, and you can click the badge or use the phone menu to turn it off.

entries.title: Real kroner prices
items: Shop prices are now real Norwegian kroner: a pølse i lompe is 39 kr, a gløgg 45 kr and a pizza 189 kr.

entries.title: Shop hours and quiet Sundays
items: Shops keep real Norwegian opening hours. Closed shops go dark, get a STENGT sign on the door and the shopkeeper goes home. The Fôr og Dyr stall closes too.
Sundays are quiet, with fewer people and cars, and the church bells ring at 10:30.

entries.title: Fast travel signposts
items: Wooden signposts now stand at 16 places around town and the valley. Walk up to one to find it, then press G (or tap) at any signpost you've found to travel between them.
Lit cairns can be travel destinations too.

entries.title: Light the cairns
items: New quest: 15 dark stone cairns (varder) stand on hilltops round the valley. Find them and press G beside each one to light it with your lantern, or with a flare. Lit cairns burn for good, and glow like beacons you can see from far away at night.
Every cairn pays something small: kr, a flare, a rumour on your map, or a story from Lykta. Light all 15 and the whole valley flares, and something on the dark mountain answers.

entries.title: Chimney smoke
items: Only houses with the fire going have smoke coming from the chimney, and there's more of it on cold evenings.

entries.title: Cold water, deep snow
items: Fall in the fjord or a river and you get cold: you shiver, frost creeps in at the edge of the screen, and a Cold badge appears. Warm up by a fire, indoors, in a car or with gløgg.
Deep fresh snow off the roads now slows you down a little.

entries.title: Windows come alive
items: Lights switch on in the evening, go dark late at night, and a few stay on.
Villagers going home light up their windows, and many windows have an advent star or a candle arch.

entries.title: Tracks in the snow
items: Footprints, paw prints and tyre tracks now stay in fresh snow, from you, the villagers, the animals and the cars. New snowfall slowly fills them back in.

entries.title: Things react when you bump them
items: Brush past a spruce and a puff of snow falls off the branches. Street bins tip over when you bump them, and get set upright again.
The playground swings and road signs sway in the wind and swing when you pass.

entries.title: Snow plough and snowbanks
items: Snow now settles on roofs and car roofs while it snows.
A brøytebil with an orange beacon ploughs the roads at night and in heavy snow, leaving snowbanks along the edges.
In the morning the neighbours shovel their driveways.

entries.title: Creaky doors and shop bells
items: Doors creak and click when you walk in and out of buildings, and the shops have a little bell over the door.

entries.title: Animals you can see on phones
items: On phones, animals now show up closer, so the evening fog doesn't hide them.

entries.title: A new film look
items: The whole game now has a moodier, more cinematic film look, with colour grading, grain, a soft vignette and edges, and tuned day and night brightness.

entries.title: Banished to Feda
items: After her speech, the witch banishes you, Chris and Martin's T3 to Feda: "Take your Chris, take your friend, and take his stupid car with you!"

You wake up at the wheel and drive the real road back towards downtown while Lykta tells you the whole story: the witch, the 24 doors, the Threshold, and what to watch out for. Expect a few surprises on the way.
The T3 finds its way back to Chris's garage afterwards. Esc skips, and Right fast-forwards.

entries.title: Food for the animals, and a food store
items: Bird seeds now sprinkle with a little sound and a spray of seeds falling from your hand.

New animal food: carrots, apples, nuts, fish, dog treats and reindeer moss. Hold one and stand still: deer, hares, foxes, squirrels, cats and more creep closer, sniff, and eat from your hand. Use drops a little pile on the ground; animals come over and eat it.
Fed animals trust you for a while: they follow you and show hearts. The moose and the wolf stay dangerous, so be careful with them.
New stall in the middle of town: Fôr og Dyr sells all the animal food and bird seeds. Marius also gets a starter set in the backpack.

entries.title: Darker nights
items: The look of day, night and dusk has been tuned, so the night can be properly dark while the lamps, windows and Christmas lights still glow.

entries.title: Brightness sliders
items: New BRIGHTNESS sliders in the LOOK section: day, night and dusk/dawn brightness, blended by the time of day, so the night can be made as dark or bright as you like.
"Night ambient" only dims or lifts the moon and sky light, so lamps, windows and Christmas lights keep glowing. Saved with SAVE LOOK.

entries.title: Giant candy canes over the fjord
items: The title cards in the opening flight now hang from garlands strung between giant candy canes standing in the fjord, with ribbons and swaying lights.
The glow behind the letters is now soft, real-looking light.
Every card hangs from the candy canes, all the way to '1. DESEMBER'.

entries.title: Smarter height fog
items: The height fog is now a real layer of valley mist: it sits on the valley floor, looks thin when you look down on it from high up, and fades away on high flyovers.
New sliders: softness, start distance, max opacity and high-view fade, and the colour can follow the sky. Mountains no longer get a grey outline.

entries.title: Sound mix
items: The town's sounds have been rebalanced: chatter, birds, animals, church bells, carols, traffic, wind, the river, music, night sounds and the witch and Lykta voices each have their own level for how often they happen and how loud they are.

entries.title: Cars with somewhere to go
items: Cars no longer drive back and forth on a loop. Each one drives to a real place, like the shop, the church, the school, the petrol station, the bank or home. It parks with its indicator on, switches off for a while, then heads somewhere new.
Some cars leave town and new ones roll in from outside. Mornings bring work traffic, afternoons bring shoppers, evenings bring people heading home, and nights are quiet.
Cars slow for corners, stop at junctions, keep their distance, flash their indicators and show brake lights.

entries.title: Townspeople with somewhere to be
items: People in town now have a daily routine. They walk real routes to real places like home, work, the shop, the church, the bus stop and the benches, go inside, and come back out later.
Mornings are busy with people heading to work, evenings everyone heads home, and at night the streets are nearly empty.
They slip on the ice, stop to chat, greet each other, turn to look at you, and kids slide on purpose.

New little moments: falling flat on their face, sneezing, checking their phone, tying a shoe, catching snowflakes, shovelling snow, snow angels, kids throwing snowballs at grown-ups, and at night some people stop, stare into the dark woods, then hurry home.
People now carry shopping bags out of the shops, and you can see the icy patches where they slip.

entries.title: More film look sliders
items: The LOOK section now has sliders for bloom (glowing lights), eye adaptation, lens dirt, height fog, contrast, saturation, shadow and highlight tint, sharpen and a letterbox mode (off / cutscenes / always).
They are all off until you move them, and they are saved with SAVE LOOK. Phones get lighter versions.

entries.title: Depth of field in the film look
items: New DEPTH OF FIELD slider in the LOOK section of the movie panel: blurs what is far from the focus, like a camera. It is off until you turn it up.
Focus can follow the centre of the screen (AUTO) or be set in metres, and it can apply only in cutscenes or all the time. It is saved with SAVE LOOK. Never on phones.

entries.title: New ATVs, mopeds, the bus and more
items: The ATV, the six-wheeler, the mopeds, the Night Wing, the bus (its doors open now) and the boats on the riverbank have all been remade with the same chunky look as the new cars.
The NCC's black SUVs have roof light bars, stripes and antennas. The kick-sled is the same as before.

entries.title: Birds that know when to be quiet
items: Birds now sing in short bursts and then go quiet for a while. They sing most at dawn and dusk, and the songbirds sleep at night.
You only hear a bird when you're near it. It gets louder as you walk closer and muffled further away.
Every bird varies its song, so you won't hear the same chirp twice in a row.

entries.title: New faces in town
items: The townspeople are new Kenney-style blocky folk: shop workers in aprons, a postman, road workers in hi-vis, nurses, police, kids in snowsuits, grey-haired grandparents with walking sticks, joggers, and everybody else in knit hats, bobble hats, scarves and puffy winter jackets.

entries.title: New cars, and Martin's Caravelle
items: Every car in town has been remade: rounder wheels with hubcaps, proper windows, lights that glow at night, Norwegian number plates, and snow and slush.
Martin's beige VW Caravelle (a T3 Syncro) with an M on the badge now stands in the right-hand garage bay at Chris's place.

entries.title: New chunky animals
items: Moose, deer, reindeer, fox, hare, lynx, squirrel, stoat, otter, sheep, horse, dog, cat and seal are now hand-built in Blender: round, chunky and a bit cute, with big eyes, in the same style as the new birds and townspeople.

Moose have the shoulder hump, droopy nose and flat antlers (bulls only), reindeer have pale necks, hares and stoats wear their white winter coats, and every animal comes in a few colours and sizes (dogs, cats and horses too).
They walk, trot and run on the same legs as before, with their feet on the ground. A wolf is in the game too, but it only shows up if you go looking.

entries.title: Solid trees you can chop
items: Trees are solid now: you can't walk through trunks or leaves, and cars hit trunks. Benches, lamps and bus stops are solid too.
Swing at a tree and it turns into real log and leaf blocks, so you can chop it down like in Minecraft. Felled trees stay gone.

entries.title: Church bells on the hour
items: The church bells now only ring on the full hour of the game's clock (no more bells at odd times).

entries.title: Nicer birds, and a bird on your hand
items: New chunky little birds with big eyes: robins with red breasts, great tits, blue tits, rosy bullfinches, sparrows, magpies, hooded crows and ravens, and herring gulls. They sing with their beaks open and puffed-up chests.
Stand still for a few seconds near small birds, and one curious bird hops closer, tilts its head, and lands on your hand. Move or look around fast and it flies off.
Bird seeds: find a bag in a chest or by a bird feeder, or buy one at the grocery or kiosk. Hold them and the birds flock to you, sometimes three on your hand. Use scatters seeds on the ground.

entries.title: The witch hates birds
items: Land a flock on the witch's roof or yard and she storms out, points, yells something rude (with a bleep) and slams the door. "Oh, there's so many birds. ████ the birds."

entries.title: The new Lykta
items: Lykta is now a little round glass lantern with brass bands, fluttering glass-petal wings and a glowing flame spirit inside with blinking eyes and pink cheeks.
She bobs, bounces when she talks, spins when she's excited and shivers when she's scared, and she flits to your shoulder when you stand still.

entries.title: Animals walk on their legs
items: The moose that crosses the trail, the hare, the dogs and the other animals now swing their legs in step with how fast they move, and their feet stay on the ground instead of gliding.

entries.title: The shrink spell
items: The witch now zaps the garden tree with a green shrink spell: it squeaks down to a tiny bonsai, still decked out with baubles, tinsel, lights and a real gold star, and she flicks it away across the snow.

entries.title: Stay off Chris's lawn!
items: People keep clear of Chris's yard, and if someone wanders onto the property, the witch storms out, points, says something rude ("Don't even think about it." "Go home." "I can see you, honey.") and slams the door.

entries.title: Notes come by mail
items: The witch's notes no longer pop up when you walk up to the house. They wait in Chris's mailbox (a red flag goes up; press G or tap it), or are now and then slipped under the front door: walk in and Chris leans down to pick it up. Esc skips, hold Right for 4x.

entries.title: Lykta quick-time moments
items: Four short quick-time moments, narrated by Lykta, play once the first time you reach the NCC gate, the witch's trapdoor, the crossing into Threshold World, the first cairn. Press, mash, hold or time the ring: win a little kr, or get a very rude comment from a lantern.
Esc skips, hold Right for 4x (tap twice for 8x, three times for 16x). Nothing ever blocks you. Marius can replay them from the movie panel.

entries.title: Chris's balcony window
items: The white window under Chris's balcony is now one of the small dark windows, and the wall around it is filled in.

entries.title: Smoke hides the names
items: In the intro, the smoke from the Eramet chimney now properly covers the name cards behind it, so Chris's name no longer shows through.

entries.title: Lykta: one line at a time
items: In the witch opening, Lykta no longer talks over herself: when she flies up to the witch she only says "Hey! Leave those lights ALONE!".

entries.title: Save your film look
items: New SAVE LOOK button in the LOOK section of the movie panel: your look, grain and lens settings are kept in the browser and, on the dev machine, in the game files, so they come back next time.

entries.title: Intro music from the first second
items: Carol of the Bells now starts on the very first frame of the intro, out over the fjord, and carries on all the way to the big title.

entries.title: Eight inflatables (and Steve)
items: Chris's yard now has all eight inflatables the witch reads out, each with a name sign: Bestefar Odd, Snø-Knut, Lille Per, Svein-Erik, Globus-Gunnar, Bjarne, Rolf and Kari.
Each one goes down its own way in the witch's rampage, and Steve the reindeer is the last one standing.

entries.title: The Panda
items: Something white watches from behind the trees in the woods at dusk and at night: a kid in a creepy homemade panda mask. Each time you spot it, it comes a little closer. Listen for twigs snapping and footsteps in the snow that stop when you stop.

After you have seen it four times, it comes for you with a knife. Dodge its lunge, throw snowballs (or use a sword, axe, sling or the lantern flare) until it drops, then finish it. The Panda mask is your prize, plus 150 kr. You can wear the mask in the head slot. Marius already has one.
The Panda is written in the animals-seen list.

entries.title: Wave bench at Hamrevarden
items: A wooden wave bench now stands at the lookout by Hamrevarden, looking out over the valley and downtown.
Builders can place more of them: "Wave bench" is in the Street and Norway lists.

entries.title: Town hall sign readable, real temperature
items: The RÅDHUS letters and the red temperature sign are no longer hidden behind the icicle lights, and the letters stay lit at night.
The temperature changes with the day, the time and the weather: coldest around 7 in the morning, mildest early afternoon, a different level each day.

entries.title: Film looks in the movie panel
items: New LOOK section in the movie panel: pick from 10 film looks (Alan Wake, Silent Hill fog, Red Dead, The Last of Us, Control, Kodak film, bleach bypass, teal & orange, pastel storybook, black-and-white noir) and set their strength.
Film grain slider, plus vignette, colour fringe, edge softness and a letterbox.

entries.title: Snow falls evenly all around you
items: Snow now falls evenly around you, even when you fly up, dive or rocket through it. No more empty layers.

entries.title: Choirs only sing
items: Choirs and carolers no longer start with a minute of band-only music: Hark! The Herald and O Come All Ye Faithful start where the singing begins.

entries.title: No cars in Chris's driveway
items: Traffic no longer drives in and out of Chris's yard (it got in the way during the witch opening). Cars still drive on the streets as before.

entries.title: Phones: memory fixes
items: Fixed a memory leak: parked cars on the parts of the map you leave are now freed (also helps when you drive a lot).
On phones, everything the intro and the witch opening loaded is cleared from the graphics memory right after them (about 7,000 pieces down to about 560), and hidden things are freed every 45 seconds.

entries.title: Lighter intro on phones
items: The intro flyover is much lighter on phones: less land built in advance, no far forest along the route, a shorter view, and the river's flow map is worked out after the intro instead of during it. Computers are unchanged.

entries.title: A longer intro from the fjord
items: The flyover now opens at the far end of Fedafjorden, drifting low over the dark water under the aurora and the moon, with DERP STUDIOS floating over the water.
Five new fly-through cards: 250+ CHESTS, 900+ SECRETS, 70+ QUESTS, 30+ ANIMAL SPECIES and 24 DOORS.
About 27 seconds longer, and the music still ends as you land.

entries.title: Cars you can hear
items: Engines hum past and change pitch as cars drive by, tyres hiss on the road and slush through the snow, and brakes squeal when a car stops hard.
The bus sighs with air brakes and doors. Cars give a polite pip-pip if you stand in their way.
Press B in any vehicle to honk (phones get a HORN button). Mopeds and ATVs buzz like proper two-strokes.

entries.title: People at home
items: Look through the windows: families watch TV on the sofa with the screen flickering in the dark, someone cooks, a kid plays on the floor, a couple dances, someone decorates the tree, and late at night someone falls asleep on the sofa.
Windows are warm where someone is home and dark where nobody is. Stand by a house and you hear muffled Christmas music, the TV, laughter and clinking dishes.

entries.title: The river flows to the sea
items: The Kvina's current now runs downhill all the way to Fedafjorden: faster in narrow stretches and rapids, slower in the pools.
Ice floes and foam drift along with it. The fjord and the lakes stay still.

entries.title: The wildlife is alive
items: Deer, moose, reindeer, foxes, hares and sheep really walk, trot and gallop now. They graze, look up at you and lie down to sleep, and leave tracks in the snow.
Birds hop, peck, take off and land on roofs, trees, lamp posts and bird feeders.

New animals: dippers on river stones, white stoats in snowdrifts, lynx eyes at night, grumpy capercaillie (back off or get pecked!), otters, seals, bullfinches and great tits at feeders, ptarmigan, an eagle owl, a sea eagle, town cats and horses in blankets.

entries.title: Downtown is much livelier
items: Up to 104 people out downtown: they stop to chat, window-shop, look up at the Christmas tree, take photos, browse the market stalls and sit on benches. Parents point things out to their kids.
Norwegian murmur and small talk until 22:30. Then it gets quiet: a few late walkers saying "God natt!", a car in the distance, doors closing. It picks up again from 06:00.

entries.title: Marius starts at the town hall
items: On Marius's login, on localhost and with ?dev=1 you start on the square facing the Rådhus, and you stay there (no more jump to Chris's house).
Dying also brings Marius back to the town hall. Chris and Martin still start at their own front doors.

entries.title: The town hall, like the real one
items: The Rådhus now looks like the real one at night: 24 red calendar doors over the windows (1–12 on top, 13–24 below).
White icicle-light curtains, the RÅDHUS sign with the red temperature display, the Sparebanken Sør sign, a glass entrance with a canopy, a little lit tree, benches and a lamp post wrapped in lights.
Mansard roof with dormers on top.

entries.title: Downtown comes alive
items: People stop in little groups on the square and in the streets and chat in Norwegian, with nods, gestures and laughs.
Passers-by greet each other ("God jul!", "Hei hei!", "Takk, i like måte!") and wave at you.
A murmur of voices where it is busy, footsteps in the snow, kids laughing, car doors, scraping windscreens in the morning; quiet late at night.

entries.title: The animals sound alive
items: Every animal and bird has its own sound now: 120 sounds for 26 kinds, from the dipper's buzzy song to the moose's grunt and the fox's scream at night.
A dawn chorus in the morning, quiet midday, owls and the eagle owl at night.

entries.title: The Eye starts off (for Marius)
items: In the movie panel the Eye is off by default on Marius's computer. Chris and Martin still have it.

entries.title: Trail life, round 2
items: 12 little things can happen on the trails: snow sliding off a branch onto you, a moose that stops and stares, an owl gliding over, a wolf howl answered closer, a skier going "Hei!", footprints that end in nowhere, a robin that follows you, Pelle the dog and his owner, and more.
4 new strangers: Sigrid the birdwatcher, Trygve the woodcutter, Solveig with the thermos and Knut the weather man.
New map layer: ANIMALS SEEN (press N, LAYERS) marks every animal you have spotted.

entries.title: Bowling carolers you can see
items: The carolers by Bowlinghallen were standing 2 m up in the air. Now they sing in front of the hall.

entries.title: Cinematic side camera
items: New driving view: "Cinematic side", a low movie-style tracking shot from the side of the car that picks the clearer side. Press V (or C in a vehicle, D-pad left on a controller) to cycle views; the game remembers your choice for driving and for flying.

entries.title: Eramet, the whole plant
items: The long storage hall, the conveyor bridge out to the quay, the ship loader, a moored ore ship, ore piles, the dome and yellow loaders.

entries.title: The valley is full
items: 889 new things to find along the trails (cairns, old campfires, lost mittens, runestones, cabins, benches with a view…) and 148 more treasure chests, all across the valley.

entries.title: Tidy car parks
items: The piles of cars on the edge of town and by the square are spread out into proper spots.

entries.title: Chris and Martin keep quiet in cutscenes
items: Their thoughts never talk over the intro, the witch or a boss, and they come a little further apart while you walk.

entries.title: Voices in your head
items: Chris and Martin now talk to themselves while you explore: a thought on first arrival at a place, after something spooky happens, on the morning a new door opens, and now and then on a long quiet walk. Each line plays once. Turn it on or off with the VO button or in the menu (Voice-over: On/Off).
The thoughts never talk over the witch, Lykta, strangers, the TV or radio, and they stay quiet during cutscenes and the film mode.

entries.title: Little surprises
items: A few deer and foxes lie asleep in the woods. Come close and they wake, stretch and wander off; they lie down again later. Listen for the snoring.
The first time you stand on a summit at night and look up at the Milky Way, the sky slows down for a moment and someone says one quiet line about it. Once per player.

Twelve nisse caps are hidden around the valley: on fence posts, benches, signs, roofs and snowmen. Look at one from close by to take it (+5 kr each). They count as "Nisse hats n/12" in your notebook and show on the big map as small caps, grey once found.

entries.title: Brighter planets
items: The planets in the night sky are now real pictures: Jupiter has fine swirling bands, a storm spot and four little moons that slowly circle it.
Saturn has a pale gold body and layered rings with gaps and shadows, Mars has a white polar cap and dark markings, Venus is a thick glowing cream disc, and Neptune and Uranus are blue-green.
Every planet has a soft glow and a very slow shimmer, and they still turn with the stars.

entries.title: Flight music
items: Flying with an elytra or a rocket now has its own music: a pulse that speeds up with you, a bright pad, and a shimmering arpeggio that only comes in above about 150 km/h.
It glides in and out as you speed up and slow down, never cuts, and over the town or the fjord it blends into that area's music.
The speech and the car radio still come first, and the M key turns it off with the rest of the music.

entries.title: The witch wrecks the whole house
items: Chris's house is now lit on every wall: the sides and the back are covered in twinkling light curtains too.
The witch opening has a new act, about 36 seconds long: she spots the rest of the lights from the sky and tears down the sides and the back.
New camera shots: a drone view from straight above, a crash zoom, a low tilted angle, a chase cam, a dolly zoom, a full circle round her in slow motion, and a crane shot.
Movie jokes: a Home Alone scream, a Gandalf slam, "We're gonna need a bigger sack", Matrix bullet time, a Titanic moment and "I'll be back" in sunglasses.
Lykta lets slip what she really thinks of the witch (bleeped), then says sorry.
Trepak, the wild music, now plays through the whole teardown, the new act included; it slows down during the Matrix moment.

Five new gags in the witch opening: she reads Chris's receipt out loud and loses it ("One light-up reindeer… named STEVE?!"), Santa pops back up and bonks her, Lykta flies up to stop her and gets swatted into the snow, she gets wrapped up like a mummy in a string of lights, and after the door slam the neighbours switch their lights off one by one (they come back on at the end).
The lights are real bulbs now, on drooping green cords, with no strings overlapping, on every wall.
A proper inflatable Santa: fur trim, beard and moustache, rosy cheeks, mittens and boots.
The intro opens with music: Carol of the Bells (US Air Force Heritage of America Band), into the title.
It snows through the intro and the witch opening, with soft round flakes.
Lykta flies with joy in the intro (hops, corkscrews, loop-de-loops) and sprinkles glitter on the town; no more lag.
The intro builds the whole valley along the flight, Feda included, and shows all the details near the camera.
Fast-forward in the witch opening: hold the Right arrow for 4x, double-tap to jump 8 s.
The witch always faces the camera when she talks now, every line checked frame by frame; no more lines said with her back to us.
Gandalf moment: she raises her broom like a staff on "You shall not…" and strikes the ground on "SPARKLE!", with a shockwave that drops the lights.
Longer, more epic Matrix bullet time; the receipt rolls 15 m down the path; her hat flops under the balcony instead of poking through it.
New lines (bleeped): "Shoo, you little glowy ████!" and "Merry Christmas, Chris, you stomping ████ ███…".
Fast-forward: tap Right once, twice or three times for 4x, 8x or 16x (intro and witch opening); Left goes back to normal.
The flyover goes straight into the witch opening: the camera swoops over Chris's house and settles on the path, no landing, no HUD in between.
Fast-forward in the intro for everyone (tap Right 1-3 times).
Eramet has its stacks now (two big ones on the tall hall, a row of thin ones and a rusty pipe chimney), and a tall steam plume the intro flies right through.
Her last words before the door slam: "Chris. If you put up any more goddamn lights… I'll sue you from here to TIMBUKTU."
The sack gets a Team Rocket ping of light too when it vanishes into the sky.
The town square tree is back in the middle of the square (it had drifted next to the town hall).
She stands still while reading the receipt, and it rolls straight down the path.
The arrival at Chris's is one smooth glide: the flyover hands over at speed, sweeps across high in front of the roof (GOD JUL in view) and cranes down to the path as the song sings its last words.
Lykta now answers the witch: "Twenty-five thousand twinkling lights! Aren't they beautiful?"
A ▶▶ button (top right) for fast-forward on phones: tap for 4x, 8x, 16x, then back to normal.

entries.title: Phone controls
items: The game now plays properly on an iPhone, sideways and full screen. Pick PLAY ON: PHONE, COMPUTER or CONTROLLER on the login screen.

Touch controls like a mobile game: a floating stick on the left (push far to run), drag the right side to look, a big JUMP button, and USE, parachute, brake and fly-down buttons that appear only when you need them.

The screen stays clear: a small map, hearts and one item at the bottom. Everything else is behind the menu button at the top left (backpack, quests, notes, case file, search, sound, graphics, left-handed mode, button size).
A how-to-play picture shows each control. The version number is shown on the title screen.
Fixed: on some phones the picture only filled the left half of the screen.

entries.title: Driving feel
items: Grip depends on the road: dry tarmac holds, packed and fresh snow let the car slide, ice is very slippery, gravel sits in between.
Steering is limited by grip at speed. On dry roads the car does not spin by itself; on slippery ground the rear steps out and you catch it with the opposite steer.
Throttle has a real torque curve with an engine note that rises with the revs, a rumble at full throttle and a short power cut on each gear change.
Braking is strong on dry tarmac and stops sooner than it slides; on ice it is long, as it should be.
The body dips when you brake, lifts when you accelerate and leans into corners. The camera swings to the outside of a corner, pulls back a little at speed and shakes over kerbs and rough ground.
Tyres squeal when they slide, and a kerb gives a thump.

entries.title: Smoother distant view
items: Far away, the valley, the snow and the rooftops no longer shimmer or crawl when you move the camera. Distant detail now melts into soft, calm colour, and the ridges and treeline stay crisp.
The lit windows of the town stay visible as warm points at a distance.

entries.title: Area music
items: The music now follows where you are: the town keeps its cozy carols, the forest gets spooky, cinematic and quirky music that changes with the day of advent, the mountains go wide and quiet, the fjord rolls with a faint foghorn at night, the NCC base is tense and dry, the witch flat is very dark, and Threshold World sounds wrong.
Areas crossfade over about 8 seconds and never cut; music still ducks when someone talks, and the car radio takes priority while it is on.

entries.title: Summit books at every varde
items: Next to every varde (and a few other lookouts) there is now a green mailbox on a wooden pole. Look at it and press G: inside is a guest book, like the summit registers on Norwegian hikes.

Read what hikers wrote before you, then write your own little entry (up to 140 characters) and sign it. It is saved with your name, the real date and time, and the game day. On a controller you can pick a ready-made phrase.

The first time you sign each book you get 20 kr, and the toast counts your Summit books. Books you have found show as small green squares on the big map (N). Friends who are online see new entries live.

entries.title: Lantern sense
items: Hold Z (or the pad's guide button, or the SENSE button on a phone) and hidden things glow through the snow: trial statues, chests (secret ones in pink), trail finds you have not found yet, NCC field sites, and a sealed rock door in the hill by the path.
Lykta glows while you hold the sense, and a little battery bar at the bottom left drains while you hold it and fills again when you let go.
Walls hide the glow. Things only light up within about 25 metres, and never more than twelve at once.
A hidden rock door in the hill: hold the sense next to it for a second and it opens into a dry passage.

entries.title: Case file
items: A new CASE FILE in the top bar (key U, and a tab next to Notes and Quests). Everything you find now goes into one file: trail finds, notebook pages, nisse trials, chests, summit books, favours for the NCC, and what the agents tell you. Each piece is a card with a little drawing.
The file shows how much of the case is solved, and three theories with a bar each. The more you find, the clearer it gets.
Visit the NCC headquarters in Hamre: the walls fill with pins, red string and photos as you go, and the agents have things to say about what you bring in.
The big map has a new CASE FILE layer, and the search finds the case file.

entries.title: Day and night, and a sky full of wonders
items: Time now passes in the valley: one minute of play is one hour of game time, so a whole day lasts 24 minutes. The clock at the top shows the game time (the date is still the real one).

It is a dark winter valley, so the day is only a little brighter than the night: a cold blue-grey twilight with a pale sun rolling low across the south, with a faint ring around it. Dawn and dusk paint a thin pink and orange band on the horizon.

A sky to look up at: stars of every colour, the Milky Way with its dark lanes and glowing clouds, a big moon with craters and real phases, and bigger-than-life planets (look for the ring of Saturn). Shooting stars streak by now and then, and a slow satellite crosses the sky.
Street lamps switch on in the evening and off in the morning, windows glow at night and are dim by day, the Christmas lights are softer by day, and the northern lights shine every night.
Christmas bulbs are now small round lights instead of big white squares when you stand close.

entries.title: Nisse trials
items: Small carved nisse statues in red caps are hidden out in the wild. Each one has a little trial: light a row of lanterns, hit the targets with snowballs, follow glowing footprints, ring the bells in the right order, or step on the carved stones.
Pjusk whispers the hint (with subtitles). Solve a trial and the statue wakes, you get a reward, and it turns grey on the big map. Find them all for a golden cap.
The big map has a new NISSE TRIALS layer (red caps) and the search finds them.

entries.title: A living, creaking world
items: The world now has its own sounds: trees creak and groan, snow slides off branches, branches snap, ice on the lakes groans and pings, far-off bells and dogs, a distant door, a swinging sign.

Out in the woods at night it gets more uneasy the deeper you go and the further you are from a lamp, a house or a fire: stranger and closer sounds, a low hum underneath, and sometimes everything goes completely quiet for a few seconds.
Safe places (street lamps, warm houses, the camp fire) calm it down again within a few seconds. By day it is gentle: wind in the spruce, small birds, sled bells, church bells.
Doors creak when you open and close them, and houses sometimes creak or rattle when you walk past at night.
New Ambience switch in the Sound menu: Off, Normal or Spooky.

Footsteps now sound like what you stand on: fresh snow, packed snow, snow-covered gravel, ice, road, paving, gravel, dirt, grass, forest floor, wooden decks and floors, tiles, carpet, metal, glass, dungeon stone, the running track and shallow water. Some are real recordings.
